stories.title: Warriors withholding payments to Porzingis, sources say
stories.summary: The Golden State Warriors are not delivering semimonthly payments to veteran center Kristaps Porzingis on his $20 million salary, league sources told ESPN, ruling that the currently absent center is not rendering his services.
stories.detailText: The Golden State Warriors are not delivering semimonthly payments to veteran center Kristaps Porzingis on his $20 million salary, league sources told ESPN, ruling that the currently absent center is not rendering his services. General manager Mike Dunleavy and the Warriors' front office are still actively pursuing trade avenues utilizing Porzingis' contract even as the 31-year-old leans toward ending his NBA career. For rival teams, absorbing Porzingis' near-expiring salary could either allow them to move a longer-term salary out to save money (plus clear a roster spot via buyout) or theoretically net a draft asset, depending on what the Warriors are willing to attach. The Warriors have no current plans on voiding Porzingis' contract, team sources said, maintaining trade flexibility up until the Feb. 11 deadline. Porzingis is not actively disputing the lack of payments and the player's association has no plan to dispute either, league sources said. Under different circumstances last season, the Miami Heat withheld payments for veteran guard Terry Rozier while he was under federal investigation in a gambling scandal but did spend the months leading up to the deadline exploring trade possibilities with his contract. After battling an elongated health issue the past two seasons, Porzingis signed a two-year, $40 million extension with the Warriors this summer (only $3 million guaranteed in the second season). But on the eve of training camp, he called Dunleavy and stepped away from the team. The Warriors gave him some space initially but expected him to return to the facility and be around his teammates and the medical staff in his recovery, team sources said. After a meeting with Dunleavy and Rick Celebrini, the team's lead medical decision-maker, in early October, the team sent out a statement declaring he would be around. It didn't last. Porzingis left the facility, hasn't returned and the organization shifted his official status from out with "general illness" (as they'd listed during his absences last season) to "not with team," a purposeful change. This is no longer described as an excused absence for the center. In his absence, the Warriors have won five consecutive games after opening the season 0-3.

stories.detailText: The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks . The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics , and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season. Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo 's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season? All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders. Quick links: Free agency grades | Trade grades Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz Depth charts | Trade machine | More Nov. 4 NBA Trade Lab updates: Porzingis is popular in mock deals In the first weeks since the release of ESPN Analytics' new NBA Trade Lab , the player involved in the most fan-created trades is Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis , who's in the news because the franchise is withholding payments from him while he's away from the team . With 38-year-old legend Stephen Curry still playing at an elite level, it makes sense that fans want to see the Warriors make a swing to bolster his supporting cast. Add to that how good rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has looked to start the season, and Warriors fans might be right to think their favorite team isn't that far away from contention in the West, especially considering the early-season injury problems for the Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves . Porzingis' $20 million salary would be a key ingredient for the Warriors to match salary in a potential trade. Below are some of the top fan-created trades involving Porzingis, as scored by fans voting from the perspective of each team involved: Trade No. 1 Warriors get: A shot-blocking stretch big in Myles Turner who could be a great fit in their motion-heavy offense to replicate some of Porzingis' game. Milwaukee Bucks get: Porzingis and a young promising player in Moses Moody , who could be more valuable for the Bucks' rebuild. Moody is recovering from a torn left patellar tendon he suffered in March. Trade No. 2 Warriors get: Daniel Gafford , who can provide rim protection and elite play-finishing. He would bolster their center depth and better exploit defenses that are stretched thin out on the perimeter drawn to Curry's gravity. Dallas Mavericks get: Porzingis and a first-round pick swap to help reset their timeline around 19-year-old centerpiece Cooper Flagg , by improving their assets in a potentially loaded 2028 draft. Trade No. 3 Warriors get: Talented 6-foot-8 forward Trey Murphy III , who can defend, draw fouls and rain 3s from well beyond the arc. At 26 years old, he also has the potential to be paired alongside Lendeborg as the wing duo of the future in the post-Curry era. New Orleans Pelicans get: Porzingis, a promising young player in Moody and two future first-round picks to cash in on Murphy's value. Doing this deal would also provide more on-ball opportunities for 2025 lottery picks Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen . Have any more ideas on what move the Warriors should make? Build them in the NBA Trade Lab , then submit your trade to let fans vote on it from both sides. -- Ben Tiemeyer Warriors withholding payments to Porzingis The Golden State Warriors are not making payments to injured center Kristaps Porzingis on his $20 million salary, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Anthony Slater. Porzingis has yet to play a game this season as he continues to deal with recurring symptoms from an ongoing autoimmune condition. Hoop Collective: What does Luka's historic start mean for Lakers? Trouble in Miami Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MaMahon to cover Luka Doncic 's historic start to the season, including if it will lead to success for the Los Angeles Lakers . They move on to discuss the growing concern with the Miami Heat and if there is a path to fix their struggling defense before moving on to the impressive starts for this year's rookie class. And 76ers' dream start Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to discuss the Houston Rockets ' 6-1 start and whether they are a legitimate title contender. They then break down why Kyrie Irving might not be traded this season if the Dallas Mavericks ' continue their impressive start to the season. Next, they check in on the injured Oklahoma City Thunder , the hot Memphis Grizzlies and the dream start for LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers . Topics: 1:01: Houston impressing with 6-1 start to season 1:45: Windy Storytime: identifying contenders 4:35: Rockets looking the part of a contender 10:23: Could Kyrie stay with the Mavs all season? 25:10: Injuries stacking up for the Thunder 32:14: Memphis playing quality team basketball 35:40: 76ers winning in clutch time early MacMahon on Kyrie's future in Dallas: "When I'm talking to executives and scouts around the league ... when the Mavericks come up, it is the No. 1 thing people are asking me about. "You know, going into the season, I would have said more likely than not, [Irving] gets moved by the deadline, but I didn't feel super strong about it. The more I see the team, the more I'm around the team, the more I think it's going to be awfully hard to trade him. "Not that there won't be a big market -- there will be, but if they've got a chance to compete for a play-in and playoff spot, I just think it's going to be really tough to move Kyrie. Also, just as much as he means to that locker room and as well as he's working with Cooper [Flagg], it was beautiful basketball. "And just basketball wise they are a phenomenal fit. And I do think there's a legitimate argument to be made for the value of playing meaningful games in March and April for the development of a superstar like Cooper, of young role players like Zaccharie Risacher , who, by the way, is doing some really interesting things -- on the defensive end especially -- and he's got a player option next year. "I think it's a situation where you can get together and handle it in the summer. It's not like you have to either move them or lose them, by this deadline." The decision will make Dadiet an unrestricted free agent next summer. Oct. 28 How Dybantsa will impact the Wizards on the court After missing the first four games of the season with an ankle injury, No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa will make his regular-season debut Wednesday, ESPN's Shams Charania reported. Dybantsa's arrival could give the Wizards one of the best starting lineups in the Eastern Conference -- which would be quite a change of pace for a team that hasn't won 20 games in a season since 2022-23. Anthony Davis has been explosive and productive through four games. Trae Young is averaging 22 points and a league-best 11 assists per game. And Kyshawn George is up to 18 PPG as he continues to make strides as an all-around NBA contributor. Add Dybantsa to that mix and there's legitimate reason for excitement in Washington. The only downside is that Dybantsa should command plenty of playing time, which could further squeeze an overcrowded Wizards rotation. Already, 2025 first-rounder Will Riley has seen his playing time crater, but he, Tre Johnson and Bilal Coulibaly are all wings who will now likely come off the bench, yet deserve the opportunity to continue their development. -- Zach Kram Haliburton to miss time with hamstring injury Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton will miss time due to a hamstring injury, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Team doctors are now gathering info on a clear timeline of return. No. 1 pick Dybantsa to make NBA debut tonight Washington Wizards forward and 2026 No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa will make his NBA debut Wednesday night against the Cleveland Cavaliers , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dybantsa had missed the first four games of the season with an ankle injury. What are the Warriors' options on Porzingis? ESPN's Anthony Slater detailed the Golden State Warriors ' options regarding center Kristaps Porzingis and his lingering health issues in a report today. [Stephen] Curry twice made sure to mention the human component, expressing sympathy for Porzingis, who has made public the lingering impact he said he still feels after contracting an upper respiratory viral illness while with the Boston Celtics two seasons ago. "We always said availability was a big factor for our team with all the guys we have out," Curry said. "It's no secret that the [center] spot is an important one for us, especially with his skill set. It's hard to talk about without keeping the humanity of it in mind. But it is a tough one to figure out." Team sources continue to express an extreme level of pessimism that Porzingis will ever play for the Warriors again, but he could end up helping the organization in another way, because his contract, which is only guaranteed for $3 million next season, could still prove to be valuable in executing a trade. Read more: What are the Warriors' options as Kristaps Porzingis remains away from the team? Hoop Collective: Disastrous injuries in OKC, Kawhi out and trouble in Miami Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Bobby Marks to cover the recent injuries to Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace of the Oklahoma City Thunder , including what it means for the team's future and if they will need to make moves to remain a title contender. They move on to the recent injury news to Kawhi Leonard and how it will impact the Toronto Raptors , before closing on the Miami Heat 's 0-4 start and Ty Jerome 's hot week for the Memphis Grizzlies . Topics: 1:35: What does the Thunder front office do now? 18:56: Kawhi to miss time for knee swelling 26:24: How concerned should Heat fans be? 34:59: Memphis much better than expected? Marks on the Thunder's next steps following crucial injuries: "I think the long term, Brian and Tim, is that you will apply for this disabled player exception for Jalen Williams. I don't think you'll get it for Cason Wallace because you have to be deemed out until June 15. And I don't think that Wallace injury will get you there. I think the Jalen Williams injury will. But that doesn't eliminate him coming back. Just because you apply for it doesn't eliminate the player actually returning. That exception will be worth $15 million. You can only sign or trade for a player in the last year of their contract. "Their biggest trade assets are those trade exceptions that were created in the Lu Dort , Aaron Wiggins , and Isaiah Joe trades that range from $17 to, I don't know, $8 million. And you can trade for players on multi-year deals. Now, threshold on this is probably $7 million, right? You're $6.9 below that second apron. I don't think there's an appetite to go in there, but I think there is an appetite to spend because they went out and did that offer sheet on Spencer Jones . That would have added to their payroll another $23 million-$24 million. "So I think that's kind of what you're looking at. You're evaluating guys in that $7-million-to-below range from a roster standpoint, but I also think you can even go north of that if let's say [Nikola] Topic is not going to be a factor this year and he needs to be part of a deal down the road. But that's the long-term picture ... You're basically just trying to hold on right now and then basically figure it out when you get to December." Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Oct. 27 Jackson out 6-8 weeks in Utah with a torn MCL The Utah Jazz announced forward Jaren Jackson Jr . is out six to eight weeks with a torn MCL. He will be reevaluated in six weeks after the injury Monday night. What Edwards' injury means for Wolves On Monday, Anthony Edwards looked like an MVP candidate as he poured in 47 points in Cleveland. On Tuesday, that dream was dashed early, as ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Edwards will miss up to two months due to right knee surgery. Minnesota can still contend this season, as long as Edwards returns healthy at the end of that projected time frame. The partnership of Edwards and LaMelo Ball was one of the most exciting elements of the new season, and the Timberwolves raced to a 3-1 start featuring three blowout wins, with an overtime loss to the Cavaliers marring their ledger. At the end of two more months, 52 games will remain on their schedule. But they won't be comfortable in the meantime. The Timberwolves have a relatively shallow roster, and their bench will be stretched thin once sixth man Ayo Dosunmu moves into the starting lineup to replace Edwards. Their two-way star's absence also reduces any margin for error with the rest of the roster; Ball is notoriously injury-prone, and if both guards are ever out at the same time, a lengthy losing streak could ensue. Edwards to undergo surgery, miss up to two months Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards will undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee that will sideline him for up to two months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Edwards has been on the injury report for the injury. He dealt with runner's knee in the same leg last season. Leonard out multiple weeks, misses return to LA Toronto Raptors forward Kawhi Leonard will miss multiple weeks due to left knee swelling, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. An MRI showed no structural damage, but the recovery will keep Leonard out of a return game at the LA Clippers on Nov. 2. Read more: NBA punishes Clippers after Kawhi investigation: Top questions Oct. 26 Hoop Collective: Opening week, reaction to key injuries and new contenders? Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to discuss the NBA's first week, including the early message the San Antonio Spurs sent, the Houston Rockets rising to be potential contenders and an 0-3 start for the Miami Heat . They then move on to some negative headlines for the New York Knicks and the drama around Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum . Topics: 0:32: Jalen Williams injury reaction 14:10: Spurs sending an early message 28:30: Rockets surging out of gate 36:24: Heat struggling at 0-3 42:46: Knicks get headlines for wrong reason 49:24: Brown-Tatum media beef 57:12: Epic scoring performance from Luka Doncic 58:59: Other interesting opening-week headlines Windhorst on what the Jalen Williams injury means in OKC: "I guess I should put my Bobby Marks hat on just because what you want in a podcast is you want analysis of this beyond just a visceral response. The Thunder have the ability to apply for a disabled player exception. But let's be honest here, they cannot replace him." "They'll replace him with what they have on their roster with Ajay Mitchell . He becomes a very important piece right now and the fact that they had to trade away multiple wings over the summer -- Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort ... It comes into play for sure, but this means Ajay Mitchell will have to have a big season and now Cason Wallace , who was just rewarded with a huge contract, those guys will be needed. And you also could see some opportunities for Bennett Stirtz , who actually I think got his first NBA basket tonight. So there's probably no team that could withstand an injury like this other than the Thunder. "They can apply for a disabled player exception, which they will certainly get. They will get, I believe, the full mid-level exception that they can use up to the mid-level exception, which is like, $14-ish million that they can use to to sign a player or trade for a player. They can only trade for a player with that exception who's got one year left on his contract. "They're a very expensive roster. That's one of the reasons why they made those trades. So I cannot see them leaning into that. They're already deep and they're very expensive. So I think it's unlikely they take advantage of that, but there is a mechanism that exists." Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Oct. 23 Hoop Collective: Luka trash talked and who made an early statement Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Anthony Slater to go over the first few days of the NBA season, including Luka Doncic 's night against the Golden State Warriors and the future of Kristaps Porzingis in the Bay Area. They move on to the vibes with the LA Clippers following their punishment and whether the Milwaukee Bucks will face any punishment for the Gary Trent Jr . contract. They close on impressive performances from the Minnesota Timberwolves and Portland Trail Blazers before welcoming in veteran NBA agent Andy Miller to break down the coaching market. Topics: 4:48: Lakers dominate Warriors to start season 6:45: Yaxel vs. Luka back-and-forth getting headlines 11:28: Kessler dream start to career in LA 14:40: Evaluating Clippers first game after punishment 16:50: Will there be punishment for the Bucks from the NBA? 19:08: What is the future with the Warriors & Porzingis? 30:10: Timberwolves impress against the Heat 36:48: After unique offseason Blazers dominate Game 1 40:58: Tough starts for some rookie stars 45:19: Veteran NBA agent Andy Miller joins the show 45:53: A significant move around the NBA 50:58: Windy Storytime: Unique Garnett contract 56:53: Analyzing a unique NBA coaching contract Windhorst on the Gary Trent Jr. situation in Milwaukee: "I will tell you that it is a frequent conversation as I talk with people around the league. You know, they're like, 'Do you hear anything on the Gary Trent investigation? Do you hear anything on the Gary Trent investigation?' It is being done by a different law firm than did the Clippers investigation. They were sort of twin investigations. "I will just say I was talking to an executive the other day and he just said if this was a pre-existing deal and let's just be honest, the word of this deal was out there in the spring. I had an executive say to me that they think, and I want to be clear, I want to be cautious, but I had an executive say to me, if this is proven to be true, then this is actually more egregious than the Clippers deal. When you think of it, the Clippers didn't get any salary cap relief for their salary cap circumvention. They were just funneling their max player more money. In the case of the Bucks, allegedly Gary Trent signed back-to-back minimum contracts and then got this $64 million deal. And over these last two years as they were trying to hang on to Giannis Antetokounmpo for dear life, they got that flexibility that they were able to put into the roster. It didn't work. "Well, I'm just saying if you're going to compare it to Joe Smith ... this is more comparable to what happened with Joe Smith if indeed they are found guilty." Slater on a Porzingis' status in Golden State: "He was around the team in the week leading up to training camp. He went to this event with Jimmy Butler in San Diego, but if you talk to players and people at that event, he wasn't getting on the court. He wasn't in the weight room. He would show up to more of the dinners and the fun stuff. "But it seemed clear right before camp that he was fading away from basketball, obviously dealing with this health issue and thinking about his future. He calls Mike Dunleavy the day before training camp, basically tells him he's not coming in to work, he's going to go deal with this health thing. "He showed up for one meeting two weeks into camp as the Warriors team was in Las Vegas. He met with Mike Dunleavy and Rick Celebrini. From my understanding, those are pretty much the only two he's been communicating with during this entire process. After that meeting, the Warriors announced that he was going to be around the team. Then he left the facility and hasn't returned and has not been around the team to the point that when we put out the report yesterday, the Warriors didn't address some of the trade speculation, but did say he will not be around the team in the immediate future. "Clearly, this is something, as you mentioned, that Mike Dunleavy's called around the league and explored." Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Oct. 21 Marks: Warriors have hurdles in a potential Porzingis deal Following the news that the Warriors are exploring deals, finding a trade early in the season for Kristaps Porzingis could be difficult. First, Golden State is hard capped at the second apron and isn't allowed to take back more salary than what is sent out. The Warriors are allowed to aggregate salaries if they are receiving less money in return. Second, since teams are in the evaluation periods of their rosters, trades are uncommon early in the season. Under the current CBA, there have only been two regular season trades in the months of October and November. -- Bobby Marks Sources: Warriors begin exploring trades for Porzingis The Golden State Warriors have begun the process of looking for trades for center Kristaps Porzingis , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Porzingis remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue that has had him questioning his future with basketball. If there isn't a breakthrough with Porzingis' recovery, stepping away from his career is possible, sources told Charania. Join ESPN's Dave McMenamin for a Reddit AMA! At 4 p.m. ET Wednesday, senior NBA writer Dave McMenamin will answer anything about the Los Angeles Lakers , the Philadelphia 76ers , LeBron James , the opening few days of the season and more! Hoop Collective: Full reaction to the opening-night games Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to react to the NBA's opening day of games, including the Detroit Pistons rallying past the Boston Celtics , the Philadelphia 76ers ruining ring night for the New York Knicks and the Oklahoma City Thunder shutting down Victor Wembanyama in a big win against the San Antonio Spurs . They then welcome Phoenix Suns owner Mat Ishbia to talk about his expectations this season as well as his thoughts on expansion and NBA Europe. Topics: 0:55: 76ers spoil ring night with win at MSG 13:42: Celtics-Pistons reaction 15:14: Detroit dominates second half to beat Boston 21:52: Suns owner Mat Ishbia joins the show 22:49: How the Suns' organization makes big decisions 26:03: Thoughts on possible expansion in the NBA 28:22: Expectations for future of NBA Europe 30:23: State of the Suns for the 2026-27 season 40:26: OKC makes statement in San Antonio Ishbia on the future of NBA expansion: "Well, I'm supportive of growing the game. So I'm pro expansion. "Obviously, it depends on the situation and making sure that it's the right partners because they're now partners with us. And the right value, but also are they doing the right things for the fans? I believe that Vegas is a market that we need to fill. I think Seattle's one. I know there's been talk about Mexico City. The way I look at it is expanding the game. The NBA is a global game. And so having 30 is a limited number. Can you get to 32? I mean, can you go that many more? So, it's like, can you grow? Can you cover a big market like Vegas? "I don't care that it's close to Phoenix. I'm excited. I think there's abundance. There's opportunity everywhere. And I'm supportive of it." Ishbia on the outlook of the 2026-27 NBA season: "First off, there's a lot more balance. The East definitely got stronger. The West is extremely strong. But let's put it aside. "There's also no tanking. So there's not five free wins, eight free wins. And in the East last year, a lot of teams really compounded that because there was about seven teams, six teams trying to lose, which is horrible for our game. NBA Adam Silver did a great job. We got rid of that. So there's no tanking. "People are going to win -- 45 wins is a hell of a season. And I think it's going to be very, very tough. And I think that might be a 4, 5, 6 seed where last year it was 50, 52 wins to get to that level. And so, I think that's not been talked about enough." Topics: 1:25: Previewing the Atlantic Division 4:32: History of LeBron and the Knicks 12:39: Windy Storytime: LeBron opening nights 16:36: LeBron's approach to ring night historically 23:42: Will the big bet from the Celtics pay off? 31:50: How will the Knicks defend their title? 43:45: What will the 76ers be this season? 45:59: How much can Kawhi elevate the Raptors? 48:58: Can the Nets have a more competitive season? 51:20: Unfortunate injury news for Ben Simmons 55:26 Steph Curry injured in open scrimmage Hahn on how to keep Karl-Anthony Towns happy this season: "I can tell you from talking to him, on-the-side conversations, not in interviews, but [him] almost pleading because, people would ask him about shots. 'You only took four shots in the first half. What happened?' And all that stuff. "And it was one time I was walking away and he kind of grabbed me. He's like, 'It's not about shots. I don't care about shots.' He said, 'I just [like] being involved.' He's like, 'I love to pass the ball. I just want to help my teammates.' And so when they moved more in that Atlanta series, which turned everything into him being a hub of the offense, he was the happiest. I'm telling you this is not propaganda, he really was. He was happy because he loves to pass. And if you see the flair with the different ways he passes the basketball and the smile on his face, he wears 32, his father's number, but it's also Magic Johnson. And he has told that story many times. He loves that. "So what Windy's saying, that's literally the truth. If you want to keep him happy, keep him involved and everything else will figure itself out." Windhorst on Stephen Curry's injury update: "I don't think that they're concerned that this knee is going to be devastating, but they've just got to protect him. "So he walks off and after the events, [coach] Steve Kerr said that it was actually his right ankle, not his knee, and that he expected to be fine. So that happened, but still a little bit alarming. "We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day. "He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that." LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets . Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books. Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade Jayson Tatum 's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate. That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship. "The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday . "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years." Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch. The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%. Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience. Williamson not where he wants to be New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player. "I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be." Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery , Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp. "I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly." Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon. It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process. A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule. "My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25. "I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed." Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season. "I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit. "In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move. Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season. "No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. "We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward." ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama , Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic . No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title: "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is." Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures" Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year" During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season. "The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder." Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers . The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right." Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer. For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key. There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract. "I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do." Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons" At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense." "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said. After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal. Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset. "This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win. "We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon. "It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. "My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood." As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram 's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season. Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year" Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day. "I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me." Curry said knee is ready to go for the season Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee. "Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with." Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions. Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise Members of the Denver Nuggets ' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic 's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason. "We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns." LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. Sept. 26 Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday. 2026 NBA offseason trade grades Sept. 25 What's next for Curry and the Warriors? Stephen Curry 's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings. The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer. By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer. Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski . The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury. James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Grizzlies waive Russell The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.title: Dumont family takes full control of Mavericks, buying Miriam Adelson's shares
stories.summary: Little will change on the ground as Patrick Dumont has been the team governor and running the show already.
stories.detailText: Patrick and Sivan Dumont have formally become the controlling owners of the Dallas Mavericks after purchasing Miriam Adelson's shares of the franchise last month, a story broken by Tim MacMahon of ESPN . The Dumonts now own 69% of the Mavericks. While this is a change at the top, it should have little day-to-day impact, as Patrick Dumont has served as team governor and been the acting owner on the ground since the day Mark Cuban sold the team to the Dumonts and Adelsons. Here is what Dumont told ESPN: "It's really about long-term investment in the city of Dallas," Dumont told ESPN on Tuesday. "The Dumont family is really committed to building what we hope is the best arena in the NBA, a really significant investment in the city that will help create the new 40-year home for the Dallas Mavericks, a great experience for our fans and inspire our team to win championships. That's really what we're focused on. We had the opportunity, and we're really excited about it." As Cuban said when he sold his majority share of the team, the NBA has become a real estate business, and what Dumont is looking to build is not just a new arena but the anchor of a much larger development. That is the trend with professional sports franchises in general, including the Dallas Cowboys. Dumont, the Las Vegas Sands Co. CEO, has experience with building and development. He didn't have experience as an NBA owner when he took over the team, and that position comes with a learning curve (a longer one for some than others). Dumont became a villain early in his ownership of the Mavericks when he approved the controversial trade of Luka Doncic to the Lakers, which led to severe backlash from fans in Dallas. Dumont told ESPN’s MacMahon he learned from those experiences. "The most important thing every day is just trying to work harder to get better," Dumont said. "It's something that really applies in life, but it's something that really applies to here. It's been an experience as a new owner in the league. Dallas is a great sports city. I think we have the best fans in the NBA, very passionate, and it's my job to make sure that we win and that we support our fans. I'm really focused on that. I've learned that there are a lot of things you can do -- sometimes they work, sometimes they don't -- but you've got to keep pushing, got to keep going." Dumont made changes in the front office, bringing in Masai Ujiri to run the show, then Ujiri fired coach Jason Kidd to bring in Dusty May. Dumont spent millions to upgrade the team's practice facilities. All of this with the idea of trying to maximize the team around Cooper Flagg, who in his second NBA season is looking elite and like an All-NBA player already. The new arena will ultimately be remembered as the one Cooper built.

stories.title: For today and tomorrow, Labaron Philion needs more minutes
stories.summary: Nick Nurse can be better with his bench.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 30: Labaron Philon Jr. #00 of the Philadelphia 76ers reacts during the first half of an Emirates NBA Cup game against the New York Knicks at Xfinity Mobile Arena on October 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Sixers are 7-1 after Monday night’s 126-107 victory against Chicago. Three of their next four games are against fellow Eastern Conference contenders in Detroit, Cleveland and Boston. Perhaps for that reason, Nick Nurse might not make drastic changes to a rotation that keeps winning. After all, the Sixers haven’t opened a playoff round at home since 2023 so locking up wins against other teams in the Eastern Conference now can only help for seeding later. However, there’s one glaring mistake with Nurse’s rotation that he needs to address. When it comes to the bench, Nurse is playing Anfernee Simons, Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope regularly. These are veterans who figure to factor into the playoff rotation as well come the spring. However, whether Labaron Philon sees the court in April and beyond or not, the rookie out of Alabama should be seeing more than the eight minutes per game he’s currently averaging. Even in a 19-point win against the Bulls, Philon played just two minutes. While Philon was drafted towards the end of the first round this past summer, now’s the time to find out what kind of player he could become. Of course, he can always grow into a bigger role next season and beyond, but should the Sixers set him on a path that’s essentially burning a year of his rookie contract? Maybe that’s a harsh way of phrasing things after only eight games, but it’s the realest way of saying Philon isn’t playing nearly enough. For context, Tyrese Maxey was drafted 21 st overall in 2020 which is just one spot earlier than Philon’s 22 nd overall in 2026. In the 2020-21 season, Maxey’s rookie year, Maxey played 15 minutes per game and started eight games. That’s a considerable uptick from the amount of minutes Philon is currently playing. Additionally, under Nick Nurse in 2024-25, Jared McCain played 25.7 minutes per game as a rookie in an injury-shortened season that saw him still start eight games. Neither of these comparisons is perfect as McCain was nearly a lottery pick having been selected 15 th overall in 2024 and Maxey would have probably been a lottery pick under non-COVID circumstances in his draft eligible season in college. Part of the reason we’re saying the Sixers have a backup center problem yet again is because they whiffed on the Johni Broome pick recently and Adem Bona doesn’t seem to have any offensive skillset. Granted, those two players were recent second-rounders by Philadelphia, but the point stands. You want to get your draft picks on the court in their rookie seasons in the regular season when your rotation should be deeper. It’s cheap production if they’re good right away, gives you more clarity on what they could develop into down the line, and would also make it easier to move off of them in trades while they still have some trade value if the early returns aren’t to your liking. In the short term, don’t we all agree Maxey could use more of a breather than what he’s currently getting? Maxey is averaging a whopping 37.4 minutes per game which is currently second in the NBA to only Denver’s Jamal Murray. Maxey’s injury history is nowhere near as lengthy as Joel Embiid’s, but that doesn’t mean Maxey wouldn’t benefit from seeing his minutes scaled back a bit. Maxey’s also doesn’t seem like the kind of player that would be concerned about various individual accolades that might not come his way if his playing time decreased. More importantly, everyone can agree Maxey needs to be healthy and full go come playoff time for Philadelphia to make a deep run. In the long term, wouldn’t it be great if Philon developed into a sixth man at the very least for this team? Remember how awful Philly’s bench was in the playoffs last year? Philon represents a long-term solution to what’s been a long-term problem for the Sixers even if it’s hard to see him ever getting on the court with long-term building blocks in Maxey, VJ Edgecombe and Jaylen Brown all at the same time. Make no mistake, winning is fun and the Sixers are doing a lot of it right now. But the best teams in every sport can fuse the present with the future and win in the current season and in seasons of tomorrow. I get it Sixers fans, the current season is probably all that’s on your mind and I can’t blame you as the Sixers have as good a chance as any other team does to win the NBA championship in 2026-27. But there’s going to be basketball played in 2027 and beyond and Labaron Philon was drafted to be a part of that basketball for Philly so this season should also be about finding out what role Philon can have within this organization’s long-term plans.

stories.title: Knicks Injury Tracker: Josh Hart listed as out for Wednesday's game vs. Bulls due to right ankle soreness
stories.summary: The latest injury news and possible return dates for New York Knicks players...
stories.detailText: Here are the latest news updates and possible return dates for Knicks players... Nov. 4, 2:10 p.m. The Knicks have ruled Josh Hart out for the team's game against the Bulls on Wednesday due to right ankle soreness he suffered in the team's win against the Nets on Monday. This is the first game Hart will miss this season and the second Knick to not be available due to an injury after bench guard Jose Alvarado missed four games with an ankle injury. Following Wednesday's game, the Knicks have a few days off before New York heads to Cleveland to take on the Cavaliers on Saturday night. Nov. 3, 8:40 p.m. The Knicks are listing Josh Hart as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Chicago Bulls due to right ankle soreness. Hart has played in all seven of New York's games this season, averaging 8.6 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 3.9 assists over 31.7 minutes per contest. As per usual, Hart filled up the box score in Monday's win over the Nets with eight points, seven assists, six rebounds, and three steals. Additionally, Chicago (1-6) is listing big men Nic Claxton (hamstring) as questionable and Jalen Smith (left finger sprain) as probable for the game. Nov. 2, 6:00 p.m. Jose Alvarado is back. Head coach Mike Brown said the point guard will play Monday night against the Nets. He has missed the past four games due to an ankle injury, having played just twice this season. Nov. 1, 7:30 p.m. Jose Alvarado is officially listed as questionable for the Knicks' home game against the Brooklyn Nets on Monday. Alvarado's potential return could mean a diminished role for backup point guard Tyler Kolek , who has shown flashes of playmaking excellence in the early stages of this season. Alvarado has averaged 13.5 minutes per game across two contests this year, with five assists to four turnovers so far. Oct. 28, 2:30 p.m. Jose Alvarado has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Bulls in Chicago. This will mark the third straight game that the Knicks' backup point guard has missed due to an ankle sprain. In Alvarado's absence, the Knicks have used Tyler Kolek more off the bench. During Sunday's loss against the Magic, Kolek had zero points on 0-for-4 shooting, but came down with three rebounds and nine assists in his 15 minutes on the court. In Tuesday's win over the Pistons at MSG, the guard had two points, one rebound, three assists and two steals in his 11 minutes, helping the Knicks to their first win of the season. Oct. 27, 5:40 p.m. Jose Alvarado will miss his second straight game with an ankle sprain as he will not feature for New York on Tuesday night against the Detroit Pistons. Alvarado last played in the team's 107-103 loss against the Boston Celtics on Friday and struggled on the court during his 11 minutes of action. He scored just two points to go along with two rebounds, two assists, and a steal, but he turned the ball over three times and finished as a minus-10. Alvarado fared better in the season-opener, scoring eight points with three rebounds, three assists, two steals, and was a plus-6 in 16 minutes. Oct. 25, 5:40 p.m. Jose Alvarado popped up on New York's injury report on Saturday and has now been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Orlando Magic with a left ankle sprain, according to head coach Mike Brown in his pregame press conference. The backup point guard is the lone Knicks player to appear on the injury report.

stories.title: Next step? Fischer says Nets hope for big return for vets
stories.summary: Are the Nets looking to trade both of their vets?
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 1: Michael Porter Jr. #17 of the Brooklyn Nets against Aaron Nesmith #23 of the Indiana Pacers during the first half at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on November 1, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Nets rebuild can probably be traced back to June 25, 2024 when Brooklyn made two trades within minutes of each other that signals half steps were over. One sent Mikal Bridges to New York for five first rounders, a first round swap and a second rounder; the other an exchange of firsts with the Rockets that brought back a first rounder and a first round swap they had originally sent Houston in the first James Harden trade. The second step was the two-year-long tank that helped the Nets get two high — although not as high as they had hoped — firsts in Egor Demin and Mikel Brown Jr. as well as five other late firsts. The hope, at least among fans, was that the losing or at least the deliberate losing would be over. Not yet, apparently, as Brooklyn is off to a 1-6 start and the two rookies have shared the court for only a few minutes. For the second straight year, the Nets are also the youngest team in the league, not a recipe for contention. Now, into the fan caldron of disappointment, Jake Fischer seemingly dropped some knowledge that would seemingly ensure a longer rebuild. Speaking to Yahoo! Sports, the writer suggested that the next step could be trying to move veterans Michael Porter Jr and/or Julius Randle presumably at the February trade deadline, presumably to a contender, for more assets, presumably more picks or maybe other assets. Scoring, already an issue, and wins would be sacrificed. “Brooklyn, I would still categorize as a team that is in more of a sell situation. I believe that Brooklyn will hope that a Julius Randle, a Michael Porter Jr. could still potentially draw some real returns,” Fischer said. “The Nets, they don’t have their draft pick this year and they’re looking to be better and compete in the Eastern Conference, take some strides forward in the East. “I don’t think they’re going to be a full sell job right now, but I do think that they are still in a position to solicit trade offers for their veterans to get draft capital, potentially young pieces back in return.” Reading carefully, rather than scanning aggregators’ headlines, reveals that Fischer isn’t making predictions that the Nets will push hard to move both. He talks about “a Julius Randle,” “a Michael Porter Jr.” not both. Nor does he specifically mention the trade deadline. Nor does he gauge interest levels on the other side. Adding to the Nets’ cache of assets, of course, does make sense from a number of aspects. If, as Sean Marks has said, the ultimate goal is a player or players who will “automatically and absolutely change the trajectory of the franchise.” then the accumulation of assets makes sense, particularly in an era where trades, not free agency, is the route to acquiring stars and superstars. Look at all the stars who moved this summer. Only LeBron James signed as a free agent and that of course was an oddity. Either of the two players would seem to be the ideal final piece for teams hoping to make a final run at a title. Randle and MPJ can put up big numbers and have. Porter Jr. also has a ring. Yeah sure, both have baggage, but their ability to get buckets is undisputed. As Basket News noted, Porter Jr. is averaging 20.7 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.6 steals, shooting 38.1% from the three-point line. In the meantime, Randle holds the averages of 20.9 points, 7.7 rebounds and 4.9 assists. Their contracts also militate for moves unless the Nets see them as part of their future. MPJ will be an unrestricted free agent come July. If the Nets don’t plan on extending him — and there’s no indication at this point that they do, then trading him for assets in the interim would be imperative. Similarly, Randle has a player option at the end of this season and he too can leave in July if Sean Marks & co. decide not to make him an offer or an offer he believes fair. (MPJ earns $40.8 million, Randle $33.3 million with an option of $35.8 million.) Of the two, Porter Jr. would seem to be the more likely to return assets. He’s nearly four years younger than Randle, although Randle is closer to iron man status, having averaged 68 games a year over the last eight. He also has proven that he can be a leader during his time at Flatbush and Atlantic. It should also be noted that any trade is unlikely to produce the automatic and absolute game-changer Marks has spoken about. More likely, it’d be the big trade before the bigger trade which might happen in the summer of 2027. One of the most intriguing but also less than concrete suggestions in Fischer’s comment is that the Nets might move away from accumulating draft picks to seeking “potentially young pieces” — that is, undervalued players on rookie deals. After all, they do have 13 firsts and 19 seconds over the next seven years. That strategy has been a key element in a number of recent rebuilds, most notably OKC’s acquisition of a young Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, in the trade of Paul George to the Clippers back in June 2019. That one trade got Sam Presti one building block after another from SGA to Aday Mara. We should be so lucky. Of course the trade deadline — 3:00 p.m. ET on February 11 — is three months away and there are few trades in the first couple of months of any season. The unofficial start of trade season is December 15 for two reasons. It’s roughly 20 games into the season when teams understand what their needs are going forward as well as the first day that players signed or resigned during the off-season can be dealt. That expands the pool of players who are available by dozens. That’s especially relevant putting together complicated, multi-team deals. Perhaps the spate of early season injuries will move things up, but it’s unlikely. So, we wait.

stories.title: Austin Reaves, Luka Dončić have been impressed with Walker Kessler’s recent play
stories.summary: The Lakers’ star-studded backcourt sounds quite happy with their center
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CA - NOVEMBER 2: Walker Kessler #14 of the Los Angeles Lakers plays defense on Giannis Antetokounmpo #7 of the Miami Heat on November 2, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images In his return to Utah on Oct. 25, Walker Kessler struggled, scoring two points (1-of-2 shooting) and committing four fouls. Afterward, he conceded that he let his emotions overwhelm him and never found a rhythm against the Jazz. Since then, he’s recorded three double-doubles in five outings — all of which have come the past three games — and averaged 2.6 blocks each night. During the Los Angeles Lakers’ win over the Miami Heat on Monday, he tallied 15 points (7-of-13 shooting), 15 rebounds, two assists and two steals. A day prior in a victory against the Toronto Raptors, he posted 16 points (6-of-6 shooting), 15 rebounds, three blocks, one assist and one steal. The second Laker in franchise HISTORY to record 16 points, 15 boards, & 3 blocks on a perfect shooting night: Walker Kessler 🫡 pic.twitter.com/6e7PHrlEWe — Los Angeles Lakers (@Lakers) November 2, 2026 Through eight games, Kessler’s acquisition has been a smash hit for Los Angeles. He’s averaging 14.4 points (69.8% true shooting), 10.5 rebounds, 2.5 blocks and 1.1 steals. “He’s a big key for us. I think when he plays good, it gives us a way better chance to win,” Luka Dončić told reporters postgame on Monday. “He just need to keep going like this. Like we told him, we have his back. Obviously, he’s not going to play every game great, but what he’s been doing, it’s helping us win a lot.” The Lakers’ success this season will continue being shepherded by Dončić, Kessler and Austin Reaves. Each of them has kicked off 2026-27 in excellent form, so it’s no surprise Los Angeles finds itself 6-2 with the league’s second-ranked offense and seventh-best net rating (plus-8.8). When those three share the floor, the Lakers have outscored their opponents by 104 points in 145 minutes while notching a 138.3 offensive rating and 105.8 defensive rating, per NBA.com. Reaves, the longest-tenured Laker, seems to enjoy playing alongside his new starting center and understands his importance. “He’s been great. It’s fun to watch,” Reaves said Monday. “Glad to have him on our team and he’s going to continue to get better every single game. But he’s been massive for us this whole year.” Kessler and the Lakers will look for a third consecutive win Wednesday night on the road against the Sacramento Kings at 7 p.m. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: Hornets' Kon Knueppel to make season debut Wednesday vs. Nets following hamstring injury
stories.summary: Knueppel missed the preseason and the Hornets' first eight games with a strained left hamstring.
stories.detailText: Charlotte Hornets forward Kon Knueppel will make his season debut Wednesday against the Brooklyn Nets, the team announced . The second-year sharpshooter has yet to play this season due to a strained left hamstring . Knueppel suffered the injury during "offseason on-court activity," the Hornets said in September. He sat out all of the preseason and the team's first eight games. The 21-year-old Knueppel was initially listed as probable for the Nets game before receiving an upgrade in status hours before tip-off. Last week, Knueppel was assigned to the team's G League affiliate in Greensboro, North Carolina, as part of his recovery. Knueppel finished second in NBA Rookie of the Year balloting last season after challenging 2025 No. 1 overall pick and eventual winner Cooper Flagg by averaging 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.4 assists. Selected No. 4 overall out of Duke in the 2025 NBA Draft , he led the league by making 273 3-pointers and shooting 43% on 673 attempts. He helped the Hornets improve to 44-38 and earn a spot in the NBA play-in tournament as the No. 9 seed, turning around from the league's third-worst record at 19-63 in 2024-25. This season, Charlotte is off to a 3-5 start and have dropped four in a row heading into Wednesday's matchup in Brooklyn.

stories.title: Warriors owner Joe Lacob ecstatic with early Yaxel Lendeborg returns
stories.summary: Warriors owner Joe Lacob is already convinced the team nailed its drafting of Yaxel Lendeborg, saying "we got this one right."
stories.detailText: After just two weeks, Golden State Warriors owner Joe Lacob is already convinced the team nailed its drafting of 24-year-old wing Yaxel Lendeborg . "Some teams never get it right, and we got this one right," Lacob told 95.7 The Game on Monday. "I was 100% sold that this was the guy we wanted in the draft." Lendeborg, who was selected by the Warriors with the 11th pick this year, has exploded onto the scene, averaging 21.5 points, 7.0 rebounds and 3.9 assists over his first eight NBA games. He had a 37-point breakout performance Sunday night, leading the Warriors to a win over the LA Clippers without the resting Steph Curry . "NBA general managers just love their 18- and 19-year-olds," Lacob told the radio station. "We've all been guilty. There are some great upsides on these guys. But this guy seemed like a champion and ready to play. Everything we thought he could be he's come in and exceeded that. He's surprised Steve [Kerr] for sure. He doesn't have any weaknesses." The Warriors have won five straight games after opening the season 0-3. Lendeborg gives them a young talent on a cheap rookie deal and appears to be a lottery hit after two of their most recent lottery picks -- James Wiseman at No. 2 overall in 2020 and Jonathan Kuminga at No. 7 overall in 2021 -- are no longer on the roster. "We've made our mistakes. Everyone makes mistakes," Lacob said. "We didn't get the draft exactly right or maybe we didn't get the development right on a couple other higher draft choices in the past. Fine. Criticize us for that. But the draft is hard, guys."
