stories.title: Ziaire Williams not sure what caused foot soreness, hopeful injury is behind him
stories.summary: Williams returned to the lineup Monday after missing the prior three games
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 02: Giannis Antetokounmpo #7 of the Miami Heat looks to pass against Ziaire Williams #11 of the Los Angeles Lakers during the second quarter of the NBA game at Crypto.com Arena on November 02, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a three-game hiatus because of foot soreness, Ziaire Williams returned to the Los Angeles Lakers’ rotation in Monday night’s 138-117 win over the Miami Heat . Although he didn’t rejoin the starting lineup, he played 15 minutes and continued his highly efficient scoring season with nine points on 3-of-6 shooting from deep while adding two rebounds, two assists and a steal. “I don’t [have an idea what caused soreness]. Kind of just flared up out of nowhere,” Williams told reporters following Monday’s victory. “But we got some of the best doctors in the world and I’m in good hands. I’m here to stay [in the rotation], hopefully, as long as I can and I feel great right now. I’ll be back out there on Wednesday.” Williams’ pestering point-of-attack defense and reliable play-finishing alongside Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves have been rather valuable for the Lakers during his five appearances this season. Throughout his career, however, he has struggled with injuries and never eclipsed more than 63 games in a season, averaging 53.8 games played across his first five years. Los Angeles will hope he’s fully past this brief injury spell and can continue providing worthwhile contributions on both ends. At the very least, he seems to have full confidence in the Lakers’ training staff. That’s always encouraging. Although the sample is small, the Lakers have fared very well with their preferred starting five of Dončić, Reaves, Williams, Matisse Thybulle and Walker Kessler on the floor; in 51 minutes, they’ve outscored opponents by 23 points. While Williams was sidelined, Jake LaRavia assumed his starting spot and that quintet has also been dynamite in its limited run, outscoring teams by 42 points in 37 minutes. Entering the year, Los Angeles’ biggest question mark within its starting group was on the wings. Through two weeks, the likes of Williams, Thybulle and LaRavia have all answered the call. With Williams now back and LaRavia also playing pretty well, it’ll be interesting to see how head coach JJ Redick handles their minutes and the lineup configurations. We’ll get another look when the Sacramento Kings host the Lakers Wednesday night at 7 p.m. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: Warriors cut off Kristaps Porzingis’ pay as $20 million saga gets uglier
stories.summary: The Golden State Warriors have stopped paying Kristaps Porzingis his $20 million salary.
stories.detailText: Kristaps Porziņģis might never play another NBA game . The Golden State Warriors also might not pay a cent of his $20 million contract. NBA insider Shams Charania made an X post on Tuesday that read, “The Warriors are not delivering payments to Kristaps Porzingis on his $20 million salary, ruling that he is not rendering services”. Kristaps Porzingis of the Boston Celtics reacts on the floor against the New York Knicks during a game at Madison Square Garden on May 16, 2025. Charles Wenzelberg/New York Post Porziņģis has been ruled out indefinitely from the NBA season due to a mystery illness , and he has openly contemplated retirement as he looks to regain his health. “Golden State is permitted to move his contract at any point before the Feb. 11 deadline even without paying him currently, and will continue exhausting trade avenues as the 31-year-old leans toward ending his NBA career,” Charania added in the X post. Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors celebrates with Will Richard #3 after a three-point basket against the Washington Wizards on March 27, 2026. Getty Images “Absorbing Porzingis’ near-expiring deal would allow a rival team to move a salary out and save money and clear a roster spot via a buyout,” he continued. The Warriors are still trying to trade the 31-year-old , despite it seeming unlikely that another team would want to trade for a player that is owed $20 million and might decide to retire. Kristaps Porzingis (7) of the Golden State Warriors drives against Denis Schroder (8) of the Cleveland Cavaliers at Chase Center in San Francisco, April 2, 2026. Getty Images The one element that provides some hope to move the big man is that he is on a juicy expiring contract. It’s unclear whether Porziņģis will challenge the Warriors’ decision to withhold his salary right now. If he decides to do so, what has already become an ugly saga could get even worse.

stories.title: Warriors reportedly not paying Kristaps Porziņģis as he contemplates NBA future
stories.summary: The Warriors aren't looking into voiding the contract as they are hoping to move him before the Feb. 11 trade deadline.
stories.detailText: Kristaps Porziņģis is reportedly not being paid any of his $20 million salary by the Golden State Warriors since he is not playing, according to ESPN's Shams Charania and Anthony Slater . Porziņģis, who is away from the team as he deals with recurring POTS (Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome) symptoms, remains in play as the Warriors seek to move the 31-year-old forward before the Feb. 11 NBA trade deadline while they continue not paying him. There are reportedly no plans for the Warriors to void Porziņģis' contract and the player is not disputing the lack of payments. He signed a two-year, $40 million contract in the summer with only $3 million guaranteed in the second season of the deal. According to Bobby Marks , the decision is costing Porziņģis $218,341 per game. Porziņģis released a statement last month saying that he was working with doctors to find a way back to better health after Charania reported the veteran was contemplating his future. According to Cleveland Clinic , "POTS is a condition that causes your heart to beat faster than normal when you go from sitting or lying down to standing up." Symptoms can vary widely from patient to patient, but Porziņģis' seem more respiratory and fatigue-related. POTS significantly limited the 7-foot-2 Porziņģis during the 2024-25 Eastern Conference semifinals against the New York Knicks, when he was with the Boston Celtics. Porziņģis averaged just 15.5 minutes in that six-game series, which ended Boston's NBA title defense, with Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla revealing after Game 5 that Porziņģis didn't play the second half because " he couldn't breathe ." Over his 10-year career, Porziņģis has played 533 games and has averaged 19.5 points, 7.6 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game. Last season, he split time between the Atlanta Hawks and the Warriors, appearing in 32 games, the fewest he's played in a season in his career outside of the missed 2018-19 campaign.

stories.title: LeBron James’ agent Rich Paul explains what 76ers offer that Lakers couldn’t
stories.summary: LeBron James' agent Rich Paul made an eye-opening comparison between the Philadelphia 76ers and the Los Angeles Lakers.
stories.detailText: The discourse around LeBron James’ decision to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in favor of the Philadelphia 76ers is still raging, despite the decision being months old at this point. James’ agent Rich Paul and Max Kellerman discussed this during a recent episode of their “Game Over” podcast. “When you’re in years 22, 23, 24, and you still have something left in the tank, it is a beautiful situation where you can position yourself alongside other guys that can play roles at a high level that give you a real chance of winning. And you don’t have to try to be someone that you’re no longer capable of being today,” Paul said. Rich Paul speaking about LeBron James playing on the Philadelphia 76ers during the “Game Over” podcast. (X/@NBA_Courtside). “What gave rise to that was a change of location. Lakers didn’t have that. They didn’t have that… That’s one of the reasons he picked Philadelphia,” Kellerman said, which Paul agreed with. Paul did give the Lakers credit at another point in the podcast, saying that they made good moves in free agency to add pieces around Luka Dončić after LeBron’s exit. Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James wears a vote shirt before a game against the Chicago Bulls at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Nov. 2, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Luka Doncic (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers talks with referee Nick Buchert (3) during the first quarter of an NBA game in Los Angeles, Nov. 2, 2026. Getty Images LeBron certainly looks to be playing with a lot of joy right now. And the Lakers are arguably playing better basketball right now than they did at any point last season, largely because of these new additions to the roster. LeBron’s decision seems to have been a win-win for both sides right now. Both teams sit in first place of their respective divisions. But there’s still a lot of basketball to be played that could change whether that remains true.

stories.title: The rise of Cooper Flagg: How the Mavericks' teenage star is leading the franchise forward
stories.summary: With the teenage star's continued trajectory, Dallas' future is much brighter than its recent past.
stories.detailText: DALLAS — Not long after an emotional NBA Cup win over the Houston Rockets on Friday, Cooper Flagg was asked about the joys of the Dallas' Mavericks' new two-star dynamic. Flagg and Kyrie Irving had combined for 68 points, 15 assists and 13 rebounds in the contest, the Mavs' third win in a row. But the 19-year-old didn't want to focus on himself or take away from his team's achievement against a legitimate contender. Flagg redirected the question to preach about players excelling in their various roles regardless of perceived status. "We have a lot of stars," he said. Such a remark can be lost in a postgame interview, especially one where the subject tends to keep things brief and direct. But in that moment, Flagg was displaying a level of leadership that is typically unbeknownst to teenagers, much less budding superstars being handed the keys to a franchise. (Mallory Bielecki/Yahoo Sports Illustration) In three months, it will mark two years since the stunning Dallas trade that sent Luka Dončić to Los Angeles in exchange for Anthony Davis. The massive void left by Dončić and the emotional toll from such a jarring move created a butterfly effect for the city and organization, ultimately leading to the drafting of Flagg, but also the firing of head coach Jason Kidd and general manager Nico Harrison, and the hiring of Dusty May and Masai Ujiri this offseason. But beauty can emerge from despair. So when May and Ujiri embraced in the tunnel after the final buzzer against Houston, hope re-emerged. And although the transition between eras has certainly come with its fair share of detours, Flagg's growing leadership in Year 2 — and, more importantly, his veteran teammates empowering him — has provided a North Star to follow. "He's taken a step into a leadership role," teammate Daniel Gafford said. "There's different ways you can lead in certain areas. With Coop, he just finds ways to have fun throughout the craziest times. Kyrie [Irving] is one of the biggest leaders in the locker room and he leads by his voice and example. Coop is following suit and taking notes and doing it himself." "It's huge," Flagg added. "Just getting the respect of my peers and teammates last year was big for me. They're trusting me, I'm trusting myself. It's a good recipe." Flagg's mental growth has been concurrent with his on-court development. In the shot clock era, there are only 20 players who have averaged 25 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists, a steal and a block per game. At 19, Flagg is the youngest ever to reach those benchmarks. Ironically, part of his success stems from the chaos he was born into. As a rookie under Kidd, Flagg was originally miscast as a point guard with questionable spacing at times, and at other junctures shared a backcourt with the likes of Brandon Williams, Ryan Nembhard and D'Angelo Russell — hardly a trio of names that screams development. Flagg also was a victim of Dallas' rotational roulette; only Cleveland and Washington had their most common lineups on the floor together less than Flagg's most consistent one (92 minutes, per NBA.com tracking data) last season. A year later, Flagg has a clear-cut role in a cleaner half-court setup and has taken lessons from his playmaking past and refined them. His processor has sped up as the game has slowed down for him, better understanding how to attack opposing defenders, crack open schemes and create the best shot for himself and those around him. As his usage rate has risen, so too has his assist rate, with Flagg now operating in the 98th and 97th percentiles , respectively, per Cleaning the Glass. An increase in possessions as a ball-handler has resulted in top-20 marks in secondary assists, potential assists and assist points created. It's no surprise the Mavericks are 17 points per 100 half-court possessions better with Flagg on the floor. Flip to a Mavs game on League Pass on a Tuesday night and you'll see Irving receive an inbounds pass, flip it to Flagg and jog to the opposing wing to let him go to work. "Just comfortable," Flagg said on how he feels with the ball in the half-court. "I'm comfortable getting to my spots and with my teammates. Coach is putting me in great spots." Dallas was one of the worst spacing units last season, but Flagg now has Irving (a career 40% 3-point shooter) and Max Christie (38%) next to him (and the hope is P.J. Washington returns to his 2024 form, where he shot 38% from deep). May also wants to play with pace and incorporates a high volume of pick-and-rolls to get both Flagg and Irving on the ball. The pace, space and freedom allow Flagg's unorthodox style to take form — more isolations , more midrange attempts and a better overall shot selection. (His 3-point efficiency, hovering around 23%, remains a work in progress, but he's been able to establish elite go-to moves that negate the need to launch unnecessary 3s into the sun.) the MOST efficient Iso floater shotmaking seasons since 2021 min 150+ total floater poss, 30+ iso floater poss. https://t.co/SMmTeLq5g3 pic.twitter.com/mB9TD5FLFE — David Lee (@dlee4three) August 16, 2026 Flagg's improved comfort within the offense speaks to his relationship with May; an open, honest one that incorporates feedback and fluidity. "It's been great," Flagg said of his bond with May. "He watched a ton of film from last year and knows my game pretty well. So just whatever he's seeing where he wants to put me, it's been working really well." Still, arguably none of this is made possible without Irving's presence, patience and poise. For starters, his gravity alone makes Flagg's job easier on a nightly basis, drawing attention away from him and opening up more space to operate. But Irving's experience, having shared the spotlight with a plethora of big names during his tenure, makes the day-to-day easier as well. For what it's worth, the Mavericks have outscored opponents by 25 points in 98 minutes that Flagg and Irving have been on the floor together. It's been less of a turn-by-turn approach and more cooperative, with Irving wanting to push Flagg to be the best version of himself. As an elder statesman now, it's about giving back to the younger generation. "It's been great," Irving said to Yahoo Sports. "In my first few years in the league, I had some good veterans — Anthony Parker, Antawn Jamison, Anderson Varejão — they were all good to me. But I was always trying to figure out what more I can do to bring to the team, and the best thing for me was being able to be honest about who I wanted to become in this league and how I was gonna accomplish it. It wasn't a solo job. I think he has a lot more patience than I did when I was his age. With the supporting cast around him, he can trust us with any information or questions he wants to ask." It takes a village to raise young players. A head coach without NBA experience forced to lean on his roster, creativity and communication. A wily, sage veteran with championship experience that is hell-bent on pouring into the next phase of NBA basketball. A community that supports and sees the full potential of an ascending superstar. There's still work to do. The Mavericks, despite their winning record, are just 18th in net rating. And it's not just their conference that remains a gauntlet; their own division — with the Rockets, Spurs and Grizzlies ahead of them — is as deep as ever. But with Flagg's continued trajectory , along with the other now-stable pieces in place, Dallas' future is much brighter than its recent past. "There's always so much room for improvement," Flagg said. "I haven't shot the ball incredibly well behind the arc. But just continuing to play at my own pace, getting better and cleaning up the turnovers. There's always room for improvement."

stories.title: JJ Redick challenged the Lakers defensively vs. Heat, felt team’s response was ‘awesome’
stories.summary: Los Angeles held Miami to 45 points after halftime
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CA - NOVEMBER 1: Head Coach JJ Redick of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the game against the Toronto Raptors on November 1, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Juan Ocampo/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Although the Miami Heat are off to a rocky, 2-5 start, they sit a respectable 13th in offensive rating and operate at a breakneck pace. It’s a style that could catch any team off-guard — and it often has over the past year or so — especially one playing the second leg of a back-to-back as the Los Angeles Lakers were Monday night. This season, Miami touts the NBA’s fastest time to shoot at 10.4 seconds per possession, according to inpredictable, and is fourth in transition frequency (18.4%), per Cleaning the Glass. In the first half of Monday’s duel, the Lakers struggled to corral Miami’s uptempo attack. They surrendered 72 points before the break and led by just seven. After intermission, they held the Heat to 45 points and pulled away for a comfortable, 136-118 victory . “We really challenged the guys at halftime. The biggest thing for us, the first thing on the scouting report was get back and get set,” head coach JJ Redick told reporters after the win. “We had multiple clips and multiple guys, after makes, running towards our hoop instead of getting back. This was not a pick up, full-court game. They want to make it a track meet. They want to play high volume early offense.” According to NBA.com, the Lakers posted a 95.7 defensive rating in the second half. Redick attributes much of that success to slowing Miami’s early attacks and containing its half-court offense, the former of which featured starkly different performances between halves. “We gave up 40 points in the first half in the first eight seconds [of a Heat possession]. We gave up, I think, 16 in the second half in the first eight seconds and they were 0.71 [points per possession] in the half court, which is [the 98th percentile], is as good as you can kind of hope for,” Redick said. “I thought the way they responded in the second half, or at halftime and then in the second half defensively, was awesome.” Despite being 6-2 with the league’s second-ranked offense and fourth-best net rating, the Lakers are just 18th in defensive rating thus far. Moving forward, they’ll hope they can parlay Monday’s impressive second half into a prolonged stretch of feisty defense to complement their abundantly potent offense. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it
stories.summary: LeBron James took fan interaction to a whole new level on Monday night.
stories.detailText: LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James is one of kind in so many ways. What he did Monday night might be the cherry on top. In the third quarter of the Sixers’ 126-107 victory over the Bulls, James decided he’d take fan interaction to a whole new level. He helped himself to a fan’s red wine. James looked for a transition pass from Tyrese Maxey, who snagged a rebound. James was behind the pass and his momentum took him into the stands, where he disappeared for a few moments. It wasn’t until another angle was shown on replay that we could see what actually went down in the darkness of the seats. James didn’t hold back giving reporters a play-by-play. “I spilled some of his wine,” he said postgame. “I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine. So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was alright.” Troy Clemons – the Sixers fan whose drink spilled – explained his perspective on the interaction with James to Kris Rhim of ESPN. “[I was] walking to my seat … LeBron crashed into me, he grabbed me, he said ‘My bad,’ my drink spilled everywhere. He took my drink from me and he basically just took a sip of it, gave it back and ran back on the [court].” Did he keep the cup? “At the end of the day he’s another man like me,” Clemons said. “I mean he’s LeBron, but at the end of the day, I threw that cup in the trash. And it’s nothing up with him, I just got a fresh drink though.” It should be noted that players are not supposed to drink from fans’ cups, but it’s rare for the NBA to fine someone for a spontaneous interaction such as this. In 2019, a similar thing happened when Mike Scott tumbled into the Bucks’ court-side seats. The Sixers star jokingly took a sip of a fan’s beverage and the NBA opted not to fine him. Time will tell if James has the same fate. If nothing else, an interaction like this just shows how much fun James seems to be having. The 24-year veteran noted the importance of finding joy in the game as he grinds through the season. “It’s a long marathon. And if you don’t find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you’re working and even though you’re locked in, then it could wear on you. So for me, especially at this point in my career, being able to just appreciate the moments, the small moments, these fans are great to us. We try to be great to them as well. By playing the game the right way, playing the game hard and then also just being showmen as well, it was a great game for us.” Head coach Nick Nurse also weighed in on the 41-year-old’s mindset coming into the season. “This summer I think he probably stated publicly that he wanted to go some place and have some fun playing. He loves the game, [it’s his] 24th year. It’s a group of guys, like I keep saying, that have been super focused in the intent of playing the right way. I think he’s a big part of that.” The vibes are high. It’s difficult for them not to be. With Monday’s win against the Bulls, the Sixers are 7-1 and lead the Eastern Conference. They’ve won four in a row and the only team they’ve lost to is the Pistons. The Sixers will face them on Wednesday to start a three-game road trip.

stories.title: ‘I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers
stories.summary: Brown is complementing Philadelphia’s stars, attacking the glass and setting a "non-negotiable" defensive standard during the Sixers’ 7-1 start.
stories.detailText: ‘I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Jaylen Brown has spent the opening weeks of the season describing the Sixers as a work in progress. He offered a similarly humble perspective Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena. His performance, however, provided the clearest look yet at how he can influence this group while sharing the floor with the club’s other established stars. Brown finished with 25 points, 11 rebounds and five assists in the Sixers’ 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls. He shot 9 for 15 from the field, made four three-pointers and did not commit a turnover. Five of his rebounds came on the offensive end, an area Brown has emphasized while the Sixers continue piecing together their frontcourt rotation. “Just a mindset,” Brown said. “Just trying to create extra opportunities for my team. As we’re trying to patch together our fives and our front line, I try to make an extra contribution and emphasis on the glass.” Brown has also been careful about how he describes his place on a roster that already belonged to Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. Maxey scored 15 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter Monday, continuing his torrid start to the season. He has led the Sixers in scoring while being the only starter to appear in all eight games. Brown is not interested in interrupting that. “Maxey’s been leading the way, 100 percent,” Brown said. “He’s been here. This is his team. Him and Joel have been here for a while, so the mindset has been to complement those guys. I’m finding my footing, but Maxey has been leading the way for sure.” Brown’s footing looked firm against Chicago. Beyond his scoring, he helped the Sixers control the glass, moved the ball within an offense that generated 23 assists during the first half and supplied the physicality Nick Nurse expects from him. “The dude is tough and he wins,” Nurse said. “I’ll take that all day long. The degree of difficulty on some of the shots he hit was really amazing. I thought he pounded the glass and got some key rebounds. Makes a lot of winning plays. Man, he’s a winner.” Brown spent the first 10 years of his career in Boston. He won a championship there, reached another NBA Finals and grew from a 20-year-old prospect into one of the league’s premier two-way wings. Moving into a new system alongside James, Embiid and Maxey was never going to be seamless. “I mean, he’s fitting in along with all of us,” James said. “We’re getting better and better. It’s not going to happen overnight. He spent his first 10 years in a system in Boston, in the city, so it’s going to take some adjustment. “It takes adjustment for him. It’s going to take adjustment for the rest of the guys that joined this franchise as well. But tonight was a great step.” James pointed to Brown’s “pressure, his shot-making ability, his rebounding ability” and his professionalism. Brown’s early influence has extended beyond his production. The Sixers entered Monday with one of the NBA’s best half-court defenses. Brown has been one of the group’s most persistent voices, stressing communication, preparation and attention to opposing players’ tendencies. “That’s the part that I care about the most as a group, not individually,” Brown said. “Having a mentality night in and night out, respecting your opponent, respecting the game, making sure that we are executing our coverages, we’re being clear in our communication and then we’re also taking away tendencies on a night-to-night basis. “Those things I just explained are over 50 percent of the battle.” Brown understands that maintaining those details across an 82-game schedule will require more than reminders. “A little bit of accountability,” he said. “You learn different guys require different things. How you communicate with each guy may be a little different, but accountability for sure and confrontation if need be. “The offense is going to be what it’s going to be, but our defense has got to be non-negotiable. That’s something I say all the time. Non-negotiable. You want to be a good team, defense is non-negotiable.” The Sixers showed both sides of their defensive potential Monday. They built a double-digit lead during the first half, allowed Chicago to score 36 points in the second quarter and then created separation after halftime. Philadelphia held the Bulls to 20 points in the third quarter before pulling away in the fourth. Brown did not celebrate their ability to raise their intensity after it slipped. “I don’t like that we have that,” he said. “It’s good that we have shown the potential, but we’ve got to keep that switch on. It doesn’t work like that where you just flip the switch. “It can catch up to us and it can bite us against a better team or on a night that we’re not being as crisp on offense. It can’t be a switch just because we’re playing a lesser opponent or whatever the case may be. We’ve got to make sure that mentality is from the beginning to end. Can’t skip any steps.” That urgency accompanies considerable optimism. Brown said the Sixers enjoy playing together. He loves when James grabs a rebound because “he’s like a quarterback,” capable of launching an outlet pass or immediately pushing the pace. The group is learning when to attack, when to move the ball and how to avoid hesitating in its effort to play unselfishly. “It’s a lot of talent, man,” Brown said. “We like each other, and we’re just kind of building that chemistry of how we can get this thing to a well-oiled machine. I think we’re taking steps forward every single day.” The Sixers are 7-1 despite Brown believing those steps remain incomplete. They have won close games, erased sizable deficits and received important contributions from different players. Brown’s performance Monday showed another version of how their pieces can fit. “We still have a long way to go to being a really, really solid, great team,” Brown said. “But we’ve been able to win some games. We started out the season great, 7-1, and you haven’t seen our best version yet. “That’s a good sign.”

stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1
stories.summary: The Sixers stayed hot Monday night, reaching 7-1 with a win over the Bulls.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers kept up their hot start to the season Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, reaching 7-1 with a 126-107 win against the Bulls. All five of the Sixers’ starters scored in double figures. Tyrese Maxey posted 26 points on 10-for-15 shooting and 11 assists. Jaylen Brown tallied a season-best 25 points and 11 rebounds. VJ Edgecombe’s 21 points were a new season high. LeBron James recorded 15 points, nine assists and seven boards. Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson had 24 points and seven rebounds. Joel Embiid (15 points, eight rebounds) had been listed as questionable with an official designation of “right foot plantar fascia injury management.” He sat out Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back for the Sixers’ win over the Hornets. “Plantar is a little bit of a come and go type of thing,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters pregame. “They’re just trying to manage it. It’s very painful, if you’ve ever had it. It can kind of come and go out of nowhere. So we’re just trying to manage the pain with that, be as smart as we can.” Nurse told reporters that Dominick Barlow is set to see a specialist Tuesday about the back injury that’s sidelined him to start the season. “He’s been on court a little bit … not a ton of moving around,” Nurse said. “I think they want to get to tomorrow’s appointment. Hopefully, it’ll be positive and we can get into his workouts a little bit.” The Sixers will begin a three-game road trip Wednesday when they visit the Pistons. Here are observations on their victory Monday: Edgecombe slamming away off the bat After Embiid blitzed a Bulls pick-and-roll, Maxey picked off Matas Buzelis’ hurried pass to get the Sixers rolling in transition and James jammed home the team’s first field goal. Edgecombe got a slam soon after James grabbed a defensive rebound and the Sixers again pushed the pace. The Sixers scored six quick fast-break points, leading the Bulls to burn an early timeout, and James’ long-distance feeds were a major asset. “If you’re open, he’s going to pass it,” Edgecombe said of James. “The main thing is just being ready. Tonight I had to run and go get ‘em. If you’re open and he sees you, he’s going to pass the ball.” Edgecombe had a dunk-heavy first quarter. He threw down his second when Dean Wade nabbed a steal and dropped off a typically selfless dish to the Sixers’ explosive second-year guard, whose slam put the team up 22-13. The Sixers have an abundance of dangerous options in the open floor, Edgecombe included. As he’s already shown with his continued clutch shotmaking, the 21-year-old won’t become anything resembling a non-factor offensively this year as a byproduct of the Sixers’ enhanced star power. Over the team’s first seven games, Edgecombe had averaged 11.3 points. He scored 11 in the first period on 5-for-5 shooting. More rough minutes for Bona Adem Bona missed a dunk early in the second quarter, which stung a bit more when Jalen Smith drilled a three-pointer seconds later. Bona remained the Sixers’ main backup center. He had a poor first-half stint overall amid a largely negative start to his third season. The 23-year-old big man played well in the Sixers’ victory over the Bucks , posting six points, 13 rebounds and three blocks. Outside of that, his season has been sparse on bright moments so far. It’s reasonable to wonder when Nurse might turn to alternatives like Jabari Walker, who played a good game Saturday in Charlotte, or try James again at the five. The Bulls outscored the Sixers by eight points in Bona’s first run, cutting their derficit to 40-38. Chicago went in front with a three by former Sixer Buddy Hield. The Sixers regained the advantage late in the second quarter. Maxey and James each were excellent as passers in the first half, combining for 14 assists and three turnovers. James fired the ball to Wade for a corner three that gave the Sixers a 60-52 lead. Sixers outclass Bulls Following a third-quarter Embiid fadeaway jumper and two James lay-ins, the Sixers were up 17 points. The Bulls cut the Sixers’ lead down to 11 points by the start of the fourth quarter. With Bona still struggling and on four fouls, Wade began the fourth at center. Bona then briefly spelled Wade before being whistled for his fifth foul and taking a seat. Embiid ultimately wasn’t needed for any of the fourth period and only logged 25 minutes. Embiid said postgame that he was not available to return to the action in the fourth and has been feeling his plantar fasciitis on the court. The seven-time All-Star’s health is clearly not close to 100 percent. “I was on a minutes restriction,” he said. “(The foot) has been going like that for the past few weeks. It’s painful. Just got to manage it. “If it flares up pretty bad, got to take a step back. We’ve been able to manage it, but it has its ups and downs.” The Sixers’ lead got as low as eight points, but Chicago did not shoot well enough from three-point range (26.3 percent) or have sufficient firepower to sustain a meaningful comeback run. The bottom line is the Sixers are in a different class than the Bulls, who fell to 1-6. As for the Sixers, they’ll wake up Tuesday morning at the top of the Eastern Conference standings. “You’ve got some of these nights where you kind of call them professional wins. …You look at the records and all that kind of stuff, but they have a lot of talent,” Nurse said. “A lot of these teams play a way that’s a little scary. It’s fast and it’s furious, lots of threes. … They’re going to keep coming at you, high-possession games. So they’re not easy games and I’m glad that we handled it professionally tonight.”

stories.title: LeBron Log No. 3: The King dishes, Caitlin Clark visits and closing time
stories.summary: James, Philadelphia’s leading facilitator, added a jersey exchange, signature celebrations and a warmup blooper to his latest week.
stories.detailText: LeBron Log No. 3: The King dishes, Caitlin Clark visits and closing time originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James’ latest week with the Sixers included his first 10-assist game with Philadelphia, his best performance with the team, a visit with Caitlin Clark, a crowd-wide finger wag and one jumper he would probably like back. Some of it belonged in the box score. The rest quickly made its way around social media. Welcome to the third edition of the LeBron Log. SAFE HANDS Throughout the preseason, the Sixers discussed the responsibility that accompanied their desire to play faster. They wanted to advance the ball before defenses could organize, but Nick Nurse was not interested in accepting extra turnovers as part of the tradeoff. When asked whether he could live with more mistakes if they came with better pace, his answer was simple. “No.” Seven games into the regular season, the Sixers have not yet become one of the NBA’s fastest teams. They entered Monday ranked 20th in pace. Their ball security has stood out. Philadelphia has committed an NBA-low 12.7 turnovers per game. James has helped organize the offense as its leading facilitator, recording 35 assists against 11 turnovers. He leads the Sixers in total assists despite playing only five games. Tyrese Maxey, who has appeared in all seven, is second with 31. James provided the cleanest example Wednesday night against the Pacers. He finished with 13 points, 10 assists, five rebounds, two blocks and no turnovers during the Sixers’ 114-109 comeback victory. It was his first double-digit-assist performance with Philadelphia. According to StatMuse, James also became the oldest player in its database to record at least 10 points and 10 assists while committing no more than one turnover. He was 41 years and 302 days old. James’ night was not flashy by his standards. He attempted 12 shots and finished fifth on the team in scoring. Still, he helped five Sixers reach double figures without surrendering a possession. The Sixers signed the NBA’s all-time leading scorer. Through the opening weeks of his Philadelphia career, he has been their leading passer. CUP BUSINESS James entered his first NBA Cup game with the Sixers possessing more tournament history than anyone else on the roster. He led the Lakers to the inaugural Cup championship in 2023 and was named the event’s first MVP after averaging 26.4 points, eight rebounds and seven assists during Los Angeles’ unbeaten run. Three years later, his first Cup game in red, white and blue produced his best Sixers performance yet . James recorded 20 points, nine rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one block in Friday’s 98-93 win over the Knicks. He shot 8 for 15 and saved two of his most important baskets for the final 70 seconds. Jalen Brunson’s three-pointer gave New York a 90-89 lead with 1:32 remaining. On the ensuing possession, James backed down OG Anunoby, turned toward the middle and sank a fadeaway to move the Sixers back in front. VJ Edgecombe extended the lead with a three-pointer as the shot clock expired. After Brunson made two free throws, Maxey drove for a layup and missed. James followed the play, collected the offensive rebound and scored the putback with 11.9 seconds remaining. The basket sealed Philadelphia’s second win over the defending champions and its first of NBA Cup group play. “Best game all around,” Nurse said. “He’s been good, but that was his best game for sure.” James has played more than 1,600 regular-season games, but his Philadelphia closing reel has officially begun. LeBron with the clutch tip-in! 👑🔥 The King came through with the finish! 😤 #LeBronJames #EmiratesNBACup pic.twitter.com/S1NLx9l1bm — NBA India (@NBAIndia) October 31, 2026 THE SHRUG AND THE WAG The fourth-quarter baskets were not James’ only memorable moments Friday. After converting an and-one earlier in the game, James broke out his familiar shoulder-shrug celebration. Edgecombe joined him, smiling as he mirrored the move alongside his 41-year-old teammate. The pair had already developed a personalized handshake featuring two taps to the head and a forceful shrug. This one came during the game. James supplied another recognizable celebration in the third quarter. Anunoby drove toward the basket with James trailing the play. James caught him near the rim and was officially credited with his fifth block of the season. He turned toward the crowd and wagged his finger. The fans joined in. Edgecombe later delivered the biggest shot of the game, and James met him with an embrace near the sideline. The two are separated by more than 20 years, but they have quickly developed a collection of celebrations. “He doesn’t shy away from the moment,” James said of the 21-year-old. “Young kid, but he thrives in the moment.” JUST A COUPLE OF HOOPERS James was not the only basketball attraction inside Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Wednesday. Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark watched the Sixers’ win from courtside and brought a small camera with her. It was the second time this year she photographed James during a game. In March, Clark served as a credentialed photographer when James and the Lakers visited Indiana. “The KING 👑 … Shot by ME,” Clark wrote when she shared those photos. After Wednesday’s game, Clark made her way toward the visiting locker room. She briefly met Maxey before speaking with James in the hallway. James gave Clark one of his No. 23 Sixers jerseys. The team shared photos of the exchange with a fitting caption. “Just a couple of hoopers.” just a couple of hoopers. 🤝 pic.twitter.com/LGHmaBaSit — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) October 29, 2026 Clark publicly expressed hope that James would join the Pacers before he signed with Philadelphia. Their mutual respect goes back further. During Clark’s first WNBA season in 2024, James compared the attention surrounding her professional debut to what he experienced when he entered the NBA directly from high school. “I’m rooting for Caitlin because I’ve been in that seat before,” James said at the time. “I’ve walked that road before.” James did not speak with reporters after Wednesday’s game, so he was not asked about their conversation. Maxey was asked about meeting Clark for the first time. “That’s just another person that I like to watch,” he said. “She cold. She nice. Seeing her today was really cool. Sometimes you try not to fan out, but it was really cool seeing her. It’s her building; she plays here too.” DANCE FIRST, SHOOT SECOND James and Edgecombe also produced the week’s most widely shared Sixers warmup clip. Before Wednesday’s game, the two danced together near the three-point line. Edgecombe moved away while James stepped back and launched a jumper. The shot hit the side of the backboard. Officially the funniest LeBron clip of all time 😭💀 pic.twitter.com/SoGGlO5DAy — FanDuel (@FanDuel) October 29, 2026 The clip spread quickly across social media. James still walked out of downtown Indianapolis with 10 assists, no turnovers and a victory. James has made more field goals than anyone in NBA history. Even the career scoring leader is entitled to one warmup mulligan.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double
stories.summary: The Sixers improved to 3-0 Saturday night by beating the Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season. Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards. The Sixers’ absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team’s matchup with the Pistons on Sunday. Here are observations on the Sixers’ victory Saturday: Wade debuts, Embiid starts in style Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James’ place. He’d missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain. The 3-and-D forward scored the night’s first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession. Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team’s offense in the early going. The Sixers’ seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man. Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead. One of Embiid’s assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter. Second-quarter struggles The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn’t enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter. Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run. Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn’t carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly. Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins’ three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead. The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they’d fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win. The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team’s transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game’s first 19 fast-break points. Star trio produces The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup. Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup. Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks’ odds of a road win. They’d all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter. Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers’ lead to 97-87. The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel’el Ware’s put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee’s deficit to 117-114. The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure. For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

stories.title: What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique
stories.summary: They play a brand of unselfish, team-first basketball you rarely see from a team loaded with stars.
stories.detailText: What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia They’re a team of superstars that don’t play superstar basketball. That’s the beauty of this 76ers team. They play a brand of unselfish team-first basketball you rarely see from a team loaded with stars. LeBron James is one of the two or three greatest players in NBA history, a four-time MVP, a four-time NBA champion, a 1 st -ballot Hall of Famer. Joel Embiid is a seven-time all-star, a former MVP, an Olympic gold medalist and a likely Hall of Famer. Jaylen Brown is a five-time all-star, an NBA champion, a career 20 points-per-game scorer. Tyrese Maxey is a two-time all-star, one of only two NBA guards averaging 27.0 points per game over the last four years. Four certified megastars on one team. And somehow they’ve figured out how to leave their egos at the front door and play smart, tough, disciplined team basketball, the style of ball you just never see on these superstar-laden teams. On offense, they patiently work the ball around, always looking for the open man or a positive matchup. You’ve got this bunch of big-name, high-priced All-Stars who are just as happy to pass the ball as shoot it. That never happens. The 76ers are sixth in the NBA in assists, and they’re one of only four teams with twice as many assists as turnovers. Smart, unselfish, patient, disciplined. When an all-timer like LeBron averages 7.3 assists per game that speaks volumes. LeBron is fifth in the NBA in assists per game among forwards, which is wild. You can see the joy on his face when one of his passes leads to a basket. When one of the greatest players in history has that mentality, it rubs off on everyone around him. Embiid hasn’t really got going yet on offense and still takes too many 3’s, but he’s also embraced the team-first mentality, and his 4.8 assists per game are more than one full assist above his career average and 4 th -most in the NBA among centers or forward-centers. And still one of the most dominating defensive players in the league. Brown is averaging 27.0 points, which you expect, but he’s also averaging 4.3 assists per game, significantly above his career average of 3.8 coming into the season. He’s fit in so well so fast you forget its his first season here. And what can you even say about Maxey? Just a beast. He’s averaging nearly 30 points per game but never wastes a possession, always makes the right decision with the ball in his hands and is still finding time to average 4.3 assists per game. With James, Embiid, Brown and Maxey, the 76ers are the only NBA team with four guys averaging at least 16 points and 4 assists per game. Only the Pacers, Magic and Raptors have three. But where we’re really seeing this group playing out of their minds is on the defensive end, where this bunch of all-stars, including two newcomers, has been astounding. The 76ers have the 2 nd -best defensive efficiency rating in the league, behind only the Pistons, who they play Wednesday night, and they’re allowing the 2 nd -fewest points in the league, also behind Detroit. Last year, they allowed 123 points per game through eight games. This year they’re at 111. They’re holding teams to 43 percent shooting from the field, 3 rd -best in the league and their lowest since 2011-12. Their 9.3 steals per game are 6 th -most. All five starters are among the top 25 players in the league in defensive rating – James is fourth, Embiid 11 th , Edgecombe 15 th , Maxey 22 nd and Brown 23 rd . How is that even possible? It’s rare to see superstar-caliber guys play as hard on the defensive end as the offensive end. Everybody on this team embraces it. They hustle, they work, they communicate and most importantly they commit to it. The biggest concern when the 76ers built this dream team was that it would be a team of individuals out for themselves, but the reality has been the opposite. In a very short period of time, they’ve learned how to play together. How to play for each other. And we haven’t even mentioned V.J. Edgecomb, who at 21 years old has figured out how to assimilate into this loaded lineup, never force anything, wait for his opportunities and make huge shots when he gets his turn. Edgecombe is at 12.7 points and 3.0 assists per game, and his numbers are understandably down a bit from last year, but if that bothers him it sure doesn’t show. And the role players – Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Jabari Walker – have each adopted the same ego-free style of basketball, supporting the starters however they need to. Nick Nurse deserves a ton of credit for getting this bunch to play this brand of hoops. It’s not easy to get any NBA player to put team goals ahead of individual goals. But he’s got Hall of Famers and all-stars doing it and having a blast along the way. They all seem to love playing basketball the right way and they seem to love playing together. The 76ers are 7-1 and looking like a real threat to win the East, and they’re doing it by playing the game the right way. By committing to each other and not themselves.

stories.title: Sixers face Pistons with chance to avenge lone loss of the season
stories.summary: The Sixers have a chance for revenge for their lone loss of the season thus far when they visit the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday night.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 25: Tyrese Maxey #0 of the Philadelphia 76ers drives to the basket during the game against the Detroit Pistons on October 25, 2026 at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Philadelphia 76ers begin a three-game road trip on Wednesday with a visit to the Detroit Pistons. It’ll be a battle of two teams enjoying red-hot starts to their 2026-27 seasons, with the Sixers coming into the matchup 7-1 and the Pistons 6-1. It’s worth noting that the Sixers’ lone loss so far this campaign came at the hands of the Pistons back on Oct. 25. The Sixers’ injury report is as clean as can be expected for this one, with only Dominick Barlow (back) and Ariel Hukporti (Achilles) on the list. For Detroit, they are still without Jalen Duren, who suffered a right hamstring strain in the second game of the season and has not returned since. They will also be without former 76er Isaiah Joe with a right hip contusion. The loss of Duren as it happened seemed like it could be something that set the Pistons back a bit, but they’ve managed just fine so far. Cade Cunningham continues to be an effective offensive engine for Detroit, posting 23.7 points and 7.1 assists per game this season and is shooting 37.0% from deep on a 6.6 attempts-per-game clip. In Duren’s absence, former Sixer Paul Reed has stepped up in taking on the starting five position. Reed has started the last five contests for the Pistons and has averaged 13.8 points, 6.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists. 1.6 steals and 1.4 blocks in that stint. Not only that, but Reed is shooting 65.0% from the floor (5.6-for-8.6) to start the year. The Sixers would love a backup center like that… Looking at team numbers, the Pistons are currently the best in the association in defensive rating at 102.0, but the Sixers are right there with them in third at 105.1. Detroit is holding opposing offenses to shooting just 41.2% from the floor, the lowest mark in the league. The best way to break through that wall for Philly may be to do exactly what they did against the Bulls (who, yes, are a much worse team than the Pistons) in getting out ahead in transition as often and as quickly as possible. Giving them time to set up defensively will only make things harder for the Sixers, who are still admittedly finding their footing at times in the half court offense — something one would hope only gets better and better with more time together on the floor. As I mentioned, the Sixers’ only loss this season so far came at the hands of this Detroit squad when they faced off in South Philadelphia over a week ago, but the context surrounding that game is worth noting as well. The Sixers went into that matchup on the second leg of a back-to-back (versus the Pistons after a day off), with both Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe sidelined. Don’t get me wrong, I’m not saying that because they’ve had some rest and are at full strength that it’ll be some cakewalk for Philadelphia tonight… but I think it certainly won’t hurt their cause. Both teams come into Wednesday on a three-game winning streak, but only one can remain near-perfect on the season after tonight. The Sixers and Pistons tip off at 7 p.m. ET. Game Details When: Wednesday, November 4, 7 p.m. ET Where: Little Caesars Arena, Detroit, MI Watch: ESPN, NBC Sports Philadelphia Radio: 97.5 The Fanatic Follow: @LibertyBallers

teamStories.summary: When the Spurs first drafted Jeremy Sochan out of Baylor with the 9th overall pick in 2022, I remember probably being more thrilled with the pick than warranted. I hardly knew anything about him, but I did know he had size and was not a guard, and that’s all I wanted. If you ignore 2019 […]
teamStories.detailText: Oct 12, 2024; San Antonio, Texas, USA; San Antonio Spurs forward Jeremy Sochan (10) in the second half against the Utah Jazz at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con When the Spurs first drafted Jeremy Sochan out of Baylor with the 9th overall pick in 2022, I remember probably being more thrilled with the pick than warranted. I hardly knew anything about him, but I did know he had size and was not a guard, and that’s all I wanted. If you ignore 2019 (when the Spurs drafted a bust power forward in Luka Samanic and a truly “small” forward in Keldon Johnson) and 2015 (when they drafted and stashed center Nikola Milutinov), you otherwise had to go all the way back to 2014 and Kyle Anderson to find the last time they drafted a player who was not a guard or small wing in the first round. (And even then, Anderson was more of a guard in a forward’s body.) As good as some of those picks were — steals with Dejounte Murray and Derrick White late in the first round, Devin Vassell as their first lottery pick since Tim Duncan — others were merely okay or even complete busts that failed to address what was constantly an area of weakness during the post-Kawhi Leonard era: size at the forward positions. They finally changed up their drafting pattern when they took Sochan, and he seemed like a great fit with the club, both by filling a position of need and bringing a sense of humor during a couple of rough “tanking” seasons. He had a good rookie season with the Spurs, making the All-Rookie 2nd Team and proving to be one of the better perimeter defenders in the league. He also had a knack for defending the rim and grabbing rebounds despite being slightly undersized when playing center. Across his first three seasons, he averaged a consistent 11+ points and 6+ rebounds on solid shooting numbers — inside the arc. A good comparison for him would be Malik Rose (the Spurs’ undersized backup big man from their first two championship teams) but therein lies the problem. Rose was ideal for that role in the 2000’s, but a power forward/undersized center without a three-point shot just doesn’t fit today’s game, and that’s where Sochan found himself. After winning the lottery and drafting Victor Wembanyama in 2023, experimentation began to figure out how to best utilize them together. There was the ghastly Point Sochan experiment in his second season (Wemby’s first), and he lost his starting spot and eventually fell out of the rotation while dealing with various injuries during his third season. Finally, by last season, it was clear he wasn’t part of Mitch Johnson’s future plans despite having good chemistry with Wemby. He requested a trade and was sent to the New York Knicks, where he didn’t play a role but at least won a championship against his former team. That would be the last bright moment in his NBA career that started promising but dimmed with time. He signed a training camp deal with the Portland Trail Blazers this summer, but despite a solid preseason, he was waved before the start of the regular season. He was then drafted 1st overall by the Texas Legends in the G League Draft (the Dallas Mavericks’ affiliate), marking a stark fall from just a year ago. At his introductory press conference, he was humble and respectful. When asked about the roller coaster of the last 10+ months, had the following to say: Jeremy Sochan with the most humble and thoughtful response to his last 10 months or so, from NBA Champion (Knicks) to a standard G-League contract (Texas Legends). – Drafted 9th overall by the Spurs in 2022, Sochan was a focal point of their early rebuild. – 2025–26 season,… pic.twitter.com/n1ZUt3fkTI — Abby Jones (@_abigaiiiil) November 3, 2026 “I think the way I grew up, my family, my parents; it’s always been like that. I could look at it negatively (the Portland situation). But when I look back at that situation, I think the two months I was there, I grew a lot. I was healthy throughout the whole training camp, preseason and open gym. So I think that was a blessing. When we got into preseason games, the minutes I got I think I used them to the best of my ability. I had good games. So what would be the point of being negative and angry for getting waived? Of course, you can look at it as that’s the NBA and I have a contract. But at the same time I have good momentum. So, why would I hold weight on something that I can’t control? And instead, be in this moment and do what I can do and keep that momentum going.” He also discussed having to let go of the past and focus on what he’s learned so he can move forward. Jeremy Sochan speaks on the highs and lows of his NBA career and how he’s trying to remain present while embracing this opportunity with the G-League. For context, the Portland Trail Blazers signed Sochan to a one-year, non-guaranteed deal in August 2026. Sochan played in… pic.twitter.com/QaNIwM1rHA — Abby Jones (@_abigaiiiil) November 3, 2026 “I think the biggest lesson for me is just being as present as possible. I keep going with this ‘presence’ because there’s a lot of things that you can’t control — in life and in basketball. Sometimes I feel like I’ve been a victim of the past where I’ve kinda held onto that, instead of acknowledging that and the just keep going. I think that’s the biggest lesson, for sure.” It has certainly been tough to watch how far the former fan favorite has fallen. Even if it was for the better, I was personally sad to see Sochan leave San Antonio (enough so that I didn’t begrudge him for getting a ring with the Knicks). He mentions being a victim of the past, and while I’m not sure what his own context is, he is certainly a prime example of a player who would have been much better off in a bygone era of basketball than he is today. Hopefully this isn’t the end of his NBA journey. While it’s odd to see a former NBA lottery pick with four years of experience enter into the G League draft, there are no experience limits, and he fit the requirement of having recently been waived from a training camp roster. Choosing the G League — as opposed to going overseas — shows that he is still very much interested in making it back to the NBA and is not ready to settle for anything less. Hopefully his signature competitive drive and determination keeps him going, and he eventually makes it back someday. He was a fan favorite for a reason, and even if the parting was mutual, I think we can all agree that we want Sochan to get another chance in the NBA, even if it’s not with the Spurs.

teamStories.title: NBA Contract Year All-Stars: 12 playing for a payday -- and what each might get
teamStories.summary: Bobby Marks selects a roster full of players with contract decisions that could shape the trade deadline and summer of 2027.
teamStories.detailText: Things you might not know about Memphis Grizzlies guard Ty Jerome , the 29-year-old journeyman averaging 28 points per game for one of the NBA's most surprising teams : Jerome played in the first 16-1 upset in NCAA tournament history, when he and Virginia were stunned by UMBC in 2018. (Jerome and the Cavaliers would win the title the next season.) He played two seasons with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in Oklahoma City . He played one season with Stephen Curry in Golden State . Something front offices around the league are surely aware of by now: Jerome can become an unrestricted free agent next summer. Jerome, a starting guard for ESPN's Contract Year All-Stars, headlines a 12-player roster full of potential impact free agents, many of whom are searching for massive paydays in the 2027 offseason. We're also providing early predictions on each player's next contract and the likelihood of getting moved by the February trade deadline. Let's run down the roster. Jump to: Starters | Reserves How we selected the roster We disqualified players who have previously made an All-NBA or All-Star team. That means you won't see potential summer free agents such as the Washington Wizards ' Anthony Davis , New York Knicks ' Karl-Anthony Towns , Miami Heat 's Giannis Antetokounmpo , Milwaukee Bucks ' Tyler Herro -- or even Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James , who holds a player option for 2027-28 -- on this list. Players with team options in their current contracts, such as the Knicks' Josh Hart and LA Clippers ' Rui Hachimura , also were not considered. After all, if a player is outplaying his deal enough to be considered a Contract Year All-Star, it is highly unlikely his team will decline the option. Finally, we have kept off potential 2027 restricted free agents, such as the Detroit Pistons ' Daniss Jenkins . STARTERS Fred VanVleet , Rockets 2026-27 stats: 12.2 PTS | 6.8 AST | 1.7 STL Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: VanVleet is averaging his fewest points per game since 2018-19 but has steadied the Rockets' offense. After missing all of last season with a torn ACL in his right knee, the 32-year-old guard is averaging 6.8 assists with only 1.0 turnovers per game. As a result, Houston's assist rate has improved from 27th in 2025-26 to 13th in the early going this season. Prediction: The Rockets will advance deep into the playoffs and re-sign VanVleet in unrestricted free agency. Despite being in the final year of his contract, VanVleet is not extension-eligible because he signed a two-year deal in 2025. How VanVleet factors into Houston's future could be determined by the franchise's finances. With Year 1 of Amen Thompson and Tari Eason 's extensions beginning in 2027-28, Houston is projected to be $10 million below the luxury tax and $19 million below the first apron. Ty Jerome , Grizzlies 2026-27 stats: 28.2 PTS | 5.7 AST | 42.1 3P% Contract status: 2027 player option ($9.7 million) Impact this season: Jerome was not a candidate last season because he played just 15 games, but the first two weeks of 2026-27 has made the 29-year-old an obvious choice for the starting 2-guard role. Jerome is shattering previous career highs, and Memphis is plus-18.2 points per 100 possessions with him on the court, per Cleaning the Glass. Prediction: If he continues to play at a high level, Jerome will decline his $9.7 million player option and become an unrestricted free agent. Because early Bird rights have been accrued, the maximum Jerome could sign with Memphis (or with another team if he is traded) is four years and $72.3 million. With eight teams projected to have cap space and another 12 with the $16 million non-tax mid-level exception, Jerome should have suitors outside of Memphis. If Jerome chooses to opt-in for next season, he becomes eligible to sign a four-year, $99.9 million extension. Ryan Rollins , Bucks 2026-27 stats: 11.0 PTS | 4.4 AST | 4.1 REB Contract status: 2027 player option ($4 million) Impact this season: Rollins is averaging seven fewer points per game than last year and is shooting 34.5% from the field and 26.3% on 3-pointers. Those down numbers, plus the fact that the retooling Bucks are 1-6, would normally preclude a player from this list. But the Contract Year All-Star selection process factors in much more than the first two weeks of the season. With Rollins averaging career highs in points (17.6 per game), assists (5.6) and rebounds (4.6), Milwaukee was nearly six points better when he was on the court in 2025-26. Prediction: Rollins declines the option and becomes an unrestricted free agent. Rollins signed a three-year contract with the Bucks in 2025 but is not extension-eligible until summer 2027; to sign a long-term pact, Rollins would need to decline his player option and re-sign with Milwaukee as a free agent. He could opt-in to his $4 million contract for 2027-28 and sign up to a four-year, $100 million extension. Michael Porter Jr ., Nets 2026-27 stats: 20.7 PTS | 7.0 REB | 1.6 STL Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Porter is averaging at least 20 points per game for the second consecutive season, but the 28-year-old forward is doing more than just scoring: His 1.6 steals per game (with 2.5 deflections) is a career high, and Brooklyn's defense is eight points per 100 possessions better with Porter on the court. Prediction: Porter gets traded to a contender before the Feb. 11 deadline. Since July, Porter has been eligible to sign a four-year, $236.5 million extension with Brooklyn. If the Nets move him, Porter would become eligible to sign for three years and $154 million with his new team. He can also elect to become an unrestricted free agent in the summer of 2027, regardless of his post-deadline future. Paul Reed , Pistons 2026-27 stats: 13.4 PTS | 6.7 REB | 65.0 FG% Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Reed has taken advantage of a surge in minutes (13.9 per game last season to 26.9 in 2026-27) following starting center Jalen Duren 's hamstring strain. Reed has nearly doubled his points per game and is shooting a career-high 65% from the field. The Pistons are plus-12.9 points per 100 possessions with Reed on the court. Prediction: Reed, not extension-eligible because he signed a two-year contract with Detroit, will hit unrestricted free agency. Reed's increased role should only boost his free agent stock as one of the top frontcourt options next summer. Nearly two-thirds of teams have at least $16 million to spend in free agency. The Pistons, meanwhile, are $24.5 million below the luxury tax but do have flexibility with the non-guaranteed contracts of Duncan Robinson , John Collins and Isaiah Joe . RESERVES Kris Dunn , Clippers 2026-27 stats: 9.0 PTS | 4.7 AST | 2.9 STL Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Dunn ranked fourth in steals last season (trailing only Cason Wallace , Dyson Daniels and Ausar Thompson ) and fifth in deflections. This season, his third with the Clippers, Dunn is averaging the second-most minutes in his career (29.7 per game) with a career-high 2.9 steals per game. The 32-year-old trails only Daniels for the most deflections this season. Prediction: The Clippers trade Dunn at the deadline and recoup one of the five future first-round picks docked after the NBA's salary cap circumvention investigation. Dunn then signs a two-year, $37 million extension with his new team to bypass free agency. Davion Mitchell , Heat 2026-27 stats: 16.0 PTS | 8.0 AST | 45.7 3P% Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Despite the Heat's 2-5 record, Mitchell is having a career year in minutes (33.5 per game), points (16.0), assists (8.0, third in the league) and field goal percentage (51.8%). And after recording double-digit assists in nine games last season, Mitchell is already up to four. Prediction: This truly could be too early. After three seasons with the Sacramento Kings and half a season with the Toronto Raptors , Mitchell seems to have found a permanent home in Miami. His next contract, however, will depend on Miami's cap flexibility. With Year 1 of Pelle Larsson 's extension beginning in 2027-28, Miami is projected to be $23 million below the tax and $32 million below the first apron. If Mitchell signs in the $15-16 million range per season, it is unlikely Miami has the full $16 million non-tax mid-level exception available to use next summer. (Because Mitchell signed a two-year contract with Miami, he is not extension-eligible during this season.) RJ Barrett , Raptors 2026-27 stats: 20.7 PTS | 6.1 REB | 4.0 AST Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: We were hesitant including Barrett, considering he is in the final year of a $107 million rookie extension signed in 2022 with the Knicks. Finances aside, Barrett has had three and a half impactful seasons since Toronto traded for him in December 2023. Barrett has averaged at least 19.2 points per game in the seasons since. Just as he did when Brandon Ingram was injured during the Raptors' first-round series this past postseason, expect Barrett to pick up most of the scoring load with Kawhi Leonard out indefinitely. Prediction: Despite being eligible to sign an extension since July, Barrett will become an unrestricted free agent. The Raptors are allowed to exceed the salary cap because of Barrett's Bird rights but face a financial crunch next season. With the first year of Leonard's and Jakob Poeltl 's extensions beginning, Toronto is projected to be $23 million below the luxury tax and $29 million below the first apron. Jonathan Kuminga , Timberwolves 2026-27 stats: 12.3 PTS | 5.4 REB | 44.1 3P% Contract status: 2027 player option ($6.4 million) Impact this season: Expect Kuminga to play a significant role with Anthony Edwards out for an extended period. The 24-year-old forward has started all eight games this season, averaging career highs in minutes (30.8 per game) and 3-point percentage. Defensively, Kuminga is averaging 1.3 steals and 2.8 deflections, and Minnesota boasts a defensive rating of 99.5 when the forward is on the floor. Two stats to monitor all season: Kuminga's 3-pointers (1.4 more attempts per game than last season) and free throw percentage (a career-low 55% this season). Prediction: Kuminga declines his player option to become a free agent for the third straight offseason. Because Kuminga has non-Bird rights and Minnesota is close to the first apron, the maximum first-year salary it can offer is just $7.2 million. That will be a non-starter in contract negotiations, with Kuminga signing elsewhere. Kenrich Williams , Thunder 2026-27 stats: 6.0 PTS | 3.4 REB | 47.4 3P% Contract status: 2027 Unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Williams likely does not make the list if Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace were healthy. But because the two starters will miss most (if not all) of the season, expect Williams' minutes to soar. In the 37 games as part of the rotation last season, he averaged 8.2 points and shot 36.3% from the floor. Prediction: With another financial crunch looming in Oklahoma City, Williams becomes an unrestricted free agent and signs elsewhere in the offseason. His salary next season starts at $6 million, comparable to the tax midlevel exception. Keldon Johnson , Spurs 2026-27 stats: 9.3 PTS | 5.6 REB | 1.1 AST Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: The reigning Sixth Man of the Year appeared in every game last season, breaking the record for points by a reserve. But in the playoffs, Johnson scored double-digits in just five of the Spurs' 16 games. This season, Johnson's touches are down nearly 20% and he is shooting 2.5 fewer 3-pointers per game, but he is making a more concerted effort to attack the basket. Through six games, Johnson had scored 79% of his points in the paint. Prediction: Until there is more clarity on the financial situation next season, San Antonio will table extension talks with Johnson. With Year 1 of Victor Wembanyama 's extension beginning in 2027-28, San Antonio is projected to be $11 million below the luxury tax and $18 million below the first apron. Even without Johnson re-signing, the Spurs are likely a luxury tax team when factoring in the 2027 first-round pick from Atlanta and a filled-out roster. Moussa Diabate , Hornets 2026-27 stats: 9.1 PTS | 9.5 REB | 1.8 STL Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Diabate has transformed from two-way player to perhaps the best offensive rebounder in the NBA. Thanks to Diabate's league-best 5.4 offensive boards per game, Charlotte ranks sixth in that category and 11th in second-chance points. Across the past two seasons, the Hornets are 37-16 when Diabate starts. Prediction: Diabate signs a four-year, $64 million extension on Feb. 8, his first day eligible. (The $16 million first-year salary is comparable to the non-tax mid-level exception next season.) Even with extensions for Brandon Miller and Diabate kicking in for 2027-28, Charlotte would still have flexibility below the luxury tax and apron.
