Why Devin Vassell has become a quiet constant for the Spurs
teamStories.summary: Devin Vassell has quietly evolved into the veteran presence for the San Antonio Spurs.
teamStories.detailText: IT'S AN OVERCAST MONDAY at Harlandale High on the south side of San Antonio, and the campus is abuzz in anticipation of the 60th Frontier Bowl, set for kickoff at the end of the week between the Indians and rival Cowboys of McCollum. In football-obsessed Texas, cowbells, tailgating and the smell of burgers sizzling over hot coals typically dominate high schools in October. So when Harlandale's boys' and girls' varsity basketball teams sat in an empty auditorium waiting for a surprise visitor, nobody knew what to expect. "What up guys?" San Antonio Spurs forward Devin Vassell said, emerging from backstage. "How y'all doing?" The room instantly erupted into applause. Finally, Harlandale's basketball teams felt seen. In some ways, Vassell said he can relate to that anonymity. The longest-tenured starter on the Spurs, Vassell usually isn't mentioned in conversations about the team's vaunted starting lineup, which also features De'Aaron Fox , Stephon Castle , Dylan Harper and phenom Victor Wembanyama . Vassell has been a three-and-D player, a near-20-point-per-game scorer, and a primary creator and shotmaker. He has played small forward and shooting guard for the Spurs. Now, Vassell mans the power forward position. When he signed a five-year, $145 million extension in 2023, Vassell became the highest-paid player in franchise history (he has since been surpassed). Yet outside of San Antonio, Vassell seems like an afterthought among the names populating a star-studded starting lineup with two All-Stars in Wembanyama and Fox and a pair of guards in Castle and Harper destined for plenty of All-Star nods in the future. "I feel like that's kind of been my whole life," Vassell told ESPN. "I wasn't a five-star [recruit], wasn't one of the big names. So, I've worked my way for everything, and I've never really cared about what anybody else has to say. I don't worry about the headlines. I don't worry about points. It's just a matter of how I can impact the team. It's been in many different ways. And I think that helped me so much for where I'm at today." Coming off of its first NBA Finals appearance since 2014, San Antonio signed veteran power forward Tobias Harris in free agency. Harris has started in 913 of his 1,033 career games over more than a decade. The club also wanted to add Harper to the starting lineup alongside its other dynamic guards. Vassell seemed likely to be relegated to a role off the bench this season, but it was never under serious consideration, even during the team's free agency discussions with Harris. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson considers Vassell to be the "most consistent person on the roster." It's a designation earned from the plethora of roles mastered over the course of a career in San Antonio that heads into Year 7. And his most important role happens off the court. "I think that's a fair statement," Johnson told ESPN. "I also think we thought of everything. But I don't know how long we gave that one a thought. I'm not saying he's the best. I'm not saying it's just on the court. I just think he's reached this level of consistency, whether it's being comfortable in his own skin, being at ease with who he is as a person, as a player. I feel he's reached his prime, which can be a little bit of a lightning-rod word, I know. But it just feels like he's so dependable in every single way, regardless of production or outcome." JOHNSON SERVED AS Vassell's player-development coach when the forward arrived in San Antonio in 2020 as the No. 11 pick. The Spurs were entering the second year of a six-year playoff drought that ended with last season's Finals run, and Johnson had just been promoted to Gregg Popovich's bench as the replacement for Hall of Famer Tim Duncan, who spent only one season as the longtime coach's assistant. Johnson handled Vassell's development and film study, providing the forward with honest feedback that was never sugarcoated while praising him for the strides he was making. Johnson's relationship with Vassell and the rest of the players who had previously played for Popovich helped him earn the team's trust. Johnson called Vassell's evolution "really fun to see and be a part of," throwing up air quotes when describing him as a shooting guard and wing earlier in his career that morphed into a player capable of guarding frontcourt opponents. Vassell and his rebounding ability are key to making San Antonio's smaller guard-heavy starting lineup work. It's worth noting that lineup was on the court when OG Anunoby tipped in the winning basket in Game 4 in the NBA Finals in June, making rebounding this season a priority. "[Rebounding] is a huge thing [in the new starting lineup]," Johnson said. "Devin's growth in that is a huge thing that is a huge part of that idea, [and] the group working. The idea of them and him being a big part of the rebounding has to happen, or it won't work." Johnson watched Vassell compete in starting lineups over the years alongside players such as Keldon Johnson , the longest-tenured Spur, as well as Dejounte Murray , Tre Jones , Jakob Poeltl , Doug McDermott, Jeremy Sochan and Zach Collins . Hall of Fame coach Popovich was still at the helm when Vassell became the highest-paid player in franchise history, just as Wembanyama started his rookie season. "My role, you know, it's changed a lot over the years," Vassell said. "My first year, being a three-and-D player, similar to Carter [Bryant's] position, DNP sometimes, barely playing. If I made a mistake, I was out of the game. My second and third year I was kind of just growing into an NBA player, starting to get in that starting role. Then, once Dejounte and all of them were traded, it was me and KJ (Keldon Johnson). We were both trying to get 20, trying to win games. Obviously, it wasn't enough." But as the years passed, the Spurs upgraded the talent, starting with a generational superstar in Wembanyama, followed by the additions of Castle, Fox and Harper. Now a veteran leader on the team, Vassell laughs when he tells younger teammates stories about how good they've now got it with Johnson running the show. "Even though Pop is not around as much as he was, he's always in my ear," Vassell said. "He's always talking to me. And I tell Dylan [Harper] and Carter [Bryant] all the time, 'Look, y'all got Mitch. He's a little bit different.' But Pop, he was always just on me, and he saw something in me that maybe I didn't even see in myself yet. That has really helped me out to this day." WEMBANYAMA HAD JUST dropped a season-high 43 points in a win over Minnesota as he searched for Vassell in the locker room. Vassell is a sought-after mentor at the team's facility and within the locker room at Frost Bank Center, often telling younger players such as Harper and Bryant, "I was once in your shoes." Four nights earlier, Vassell passed for a team-high eight assists in an Oct. 27 victory against Sacramento. Afterward, he quietly counseled Bryant in front of their adjacent lockers after they finished dressing. Fox -- one stall over next to Carter on the left -- was standing within earshot listening to the conversation about overcoming the urge to overthink situations on the court. Bryant said he wanted to "keep learning from him as long as he's willing to teach me." The second-year forward added that he receives a mix of tough love and encouragement from Vassell, whether that's off the court "just chilling," on the court in games and practices, or on team flights. "Devin's increase in leadership, it coincides with our increase as a contender," Wembanyama said. "He embodies our progress." Vassell's maturity was on display as the Spurs notched their third win of the season in an overtime victory over the Jazz. Vassell shot just 2-of-9 over the first three quarters that night but poured in 17 of his 21 points in the second half, connecting on 4 of 5 shots in the fourth quarter. Then, in overtime, Vassell hit a 10-footer before logging a two-handed putback jam with 1:53 left after Josh Green blocked a Harper layup. "He was [2]-for-9 going into the fourth quarter," Johnson said. "But he was playing the game appropriately. Next thing you know, he kind of helped walk the game down. On the surface level, it's like, 'Oh, he's going to play off Victor, Fox, Steph and Dylan.' Next thing you know, we're running action for him to close the game. You have to have mental toughness to go back and forth ... of this 'role' that you're playing at the given time." San Antonio embarked on a 12-0 run to put away the game. Vassell scored 12 points in the fourth quarter and overtime. "His years of being here give him this feeling of being sure of what he does," Wembanyama said. "He is sure of what he does, but we are also sure. We've got full trust in him. We like the ball to find him in these moments." Perhaps more importantly, Vassell personifies the selflessness needed for this young San Antonio squad to ascend to the next level. The 26-year-old averaged 13.9 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.5 assists during the regular season in 2025-26. In 23 playoff outings, he averaged 13.0 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.7 assists while drawing the responsibility of guarding Karl-Anthony Towns in the Finals. "Dev became probably my favorite player in the NBA after last year," Bryant said. "I hit him after the season. I was like, 'I have so much respect for you.' If Dev was on any other team in the NBA, he'd be a 20-to-25 points a night guy. Easily. He's so skilled, so talented. The sacrifices he took for us to make that next step as a team [have] been amazing." The veteran showcased that same selflessness and mentorship in the auditorium at Harlandale High in October. Seconds after he addressed the basketball teams, Vassell's mother, Cynthia, yanked a maroon flag from a long table to reveal stacks of orange and hot pink Nike boxes. Vassell had gifted the boys' team pairs of Devin Booker 's signature shoe, the Book 2, in silver and black to start its basketball season. The girls received pairs of A'ja Wilson 's A'Two shoe. Vassell also presented a $10,000 check. Soon after, he would depart through the courtyard at Harlandale toward a Lamborghini truck wrapped in a color-shifting film he described as "just depends on what your eye can see," with students scurrying from around buildings with phones in hand itching to snap a photo of a bona fide NBA player. To the students, Vassell wasn't just the "other" Spurs starter. But that doesn't mean he's uncomfortable stepping back into anonymity for San Antonio to secure the ultimate prize that eluded the club in last season's Finals. "People always ask me, 'What do you want to average?'" he said. "It's hard to say when you have so many great players on your team. There's probably four or five of us [who could average 20 points]. But that's not what we need. We just need somebody who comes in every day and helps the team out however it needs. That's what I've been."

Game Preview: San Antonio Spurs vs. Dallas Mavericks
teamStories.summary: The Spurs will be looking for their sixth straight win when they visit Copper Flagg, Kyrie Irving, and the Mavericks.
teamStories.detailText: The Spurs will look to keep their winning streak alive the Mavericks pay a visit. The two teams faced each other once already in this young season, but Dallas was without its two best players and simply couldn't keep up in the fourth quarter against a more talented opponent. Things could be different this time around. Cooper Flagg has looked like a superstar in his second season, averaging 25-6-6 and showing the type of maturity that is not common in players his age. He's coming off a poor performance in a loss against the Kings, but his ceiling seems unlimited, and his production makes him a problem on a nightly basis. Kyrie Irving missed the game against Sacramento, as he's sitting out occasionally while he recovers from knee surgery, but the veteran point guard is averaging 21 points and five assists, and seems like the perfect partner for the developing Flagg. Both should be available on Tuesday, so it should be a competitive matchup. While the Mavs have been solid this season, currently boasting a winning record, the Spurs are the hottest team in the league right now. After dropping their first two games, they have prevailed in their next five despite still trying to figure out their rotations, in part thanks to a fantastic stretch by Victor Wembanyama. They clearly have the talent to contend and should be considered the favorite over Dallas, but Flagg could present problems for a San Antonio team that starts a really small unit. On the other hand, the three-guard lineup could give the Mavericks fits on the perimeter while Wemby, looking for a bounceback performance after looking mortal against Utah, controls the paint en route to another victory. San Antonio Spurs ( 5 -2) vs. Dallas Mavericks (4-3) November 4th, 2026 | 8:30 PM CT Watch: ESPN | Listen: WOAI (1200 AM) Spurs Injuries : Tobias Harris – Out (calf), Jayden Quaintance – Out (knee). Mavericks Injuries: Santi Aldama — Doubtful (Knee), Tarik Biberović — Out (Heel), Max Christie — Out (Hip), Sergio de Larrea — Out (Knee), Dereck Lively II — Out (Foot). What to watch for The battle of the young superstars Flagg is just in his second season, but judging by his recent performances, he seems on his way to superstardom sooner rather than later. The 19-year-old forward can do it all already, except consistently shoot from outside, and should only continue to get better. He has as good a case as anyone to be considered Wemby's biggest challenger for best player in the world in the near future, so it will be interesting to see what he can do against the most dominant defensive force in the league. As mentioned, the Spurs don't have someone who can match up well with Flagg, at least physically, in their starting lineup, but Stephon Castle has shown he can bother bigger guys, and the big guy will be behind him to back him up. San Antonio can win without Wembanyama playing at his highest level, but everything is easier when their best player dominates. He could do that against the Daniel Gafford – Morez Johnson Jr. duo, and he could definitely take advantage of Dusty May going small, like he did a couple of times, to terrible results, in their first matchup. Wemby won't likely be guarded by Flagg for long, if at all, and vice versa, but whoever outplays the other could determine who emerges as the winner on Tuesday. Elite transition offense vs. elite transition defense While the halfcourt battle will be interesting to watch, whichever team can control the transition game will have a huge advantage. The Spurs play at an average pace, but they lead the league in fastbreak points. Whenever San Antonio gets to run, the offense gets supercharged, and even lineups lacking shooting become viable. It might be hard to get a huge advantage on the break, however, since the Mavericks allow the fourth-fewest fastbreak points in the league despite turning the ball over at a high rate. Dallas also prefers to play at a leisurely pace, so making sure they are forcing San Antonio into a halfcourt battle will likely be a priority for them. In the first matchup between the two teams, the Mavs actually outscored the Spurs in transition, but it seemed like it was in part because, missing both Flagg and Irving, they just took every opportunity they could to run, as it was the only way they could score consistently. The Silver and Black also seemed to play down to their opponent at times, with some bad transition defense showing their lack of focus. That shouldn't happen again, or it could cost San Antonio a win. Who will be the X-Factor for the Mavs? The Spurs are more talented than the Mavericks overall, but they have at times found themselves lacking a spark outside of their main guys. The Mavericks, meanwhile, recently had great performances off the bench by Walter Clayton Jr., who dropped 20 on the Kings, and Morez Johnson Jr., who had 13 on just five shots against Sacramento. They have also had good showings from former No.1 overall pick Zaccharie Risacher and Naji Marshall this season. One of those players will likely have to take Max Christie's starting spot, but they still have a bunch of guys who might not be dependable every night but can make an impact on any given game, as the Spurs learned while they were getting torched by the now-injured Sergio de Larrea in their first game against the Mavs. The goal, clearly, will be to limit Irving and Flagg, but San Antonio will also have to keep an eye on the supporting cast to prevent someone from becoming an unlikely hero. If you'd like to, you may follow along with the game on our Twitter profile (@poundingtherock) or visit our Game Thread!

teamStories.title: NBA Power Rankings: Summing up all 30 teams' starts
teamStories.summary: Here's where all 30 NBA teams rank after two weeks of action, plus the four words used to describe how each team has started the season.
teamStories.detailText: Just two weeks into the NBA season, storylines have been flipped as injuries and surprise surges reverberate around the league. The Philadelphia 76ers have dominated their opponents early -- and are having some fun in the process. Meanwhile, the reigning champion New York Knicks are attempting to claw themselves back into the top echelon after starting the season 0-3. It's in the West where things have started to heat up. The Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves are dealing with injuries to their stars, making way for players such as the Memphis Grizzlies ' Ty Jerome to have an early impact in his team's standings. The Los Angeles Lakers ' Luka Doncic is making an early MVP case and doesn't seem to be slowing down after scoring 42 and 45 points in his past two games. And the Portland Trail Blazers , sans Ja Morant as he deals with an injury , are showing that depth is what will set teams apart across the league. In our second iteration of Power Rankings since the season started, our NBA insiders assigned four words to describe each team's start to 2026-27, and break down why things are -- or are not -- working. Note: Team rankings are based on where members of our panel (ESPN's Jamal Collier, Michael C. Wright, Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Ben Golliver, Kris Rhim and Anthony Slater) think teams belong. Previous rankings: Preseason | Oct. 28 Jump to a team: ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS 1. Houston Rockets 2026-27 record: 7-1 Previous ranking: 4 Next games: vs. MIN (Nov. 4), @ PHX (Nov. 7), vs. DEN (Nov. 9) VanVleet's impact is immeasurable . The Rockets navigated the choppy waters of Kevin Durant 's first season nearly rudderless without floor general Fred VanVleet , who sustained a season-ending knee injury before the start of training camp. Now that he's back , Houston is a calmer, more organized team. VanVleet directs traffic, manipulates defenses to set up teammates for shots in their preferred spots and limits turnovers, catalyzing a Houston offense with the league's best rating (121.2). Wisely, the Rockets added ballhandling insurance with another veteran point guard in Marcus Smart , who can start in VanVleet's place when he sits the second night of back-to-backs. -- Michael C. Wright 2. Detroit Pistons 2026-27 record: 6-1 Previous ranking: 3 Next games: vs. PHI (Nov. 4), vs. LAL (Nov. 8), vs. WAS (Nov. 9) 3-pointers have improved. The Pistons have developed a reputation for stifling defense and it hasn't changed, being first in points per game against and defensive rating. What has seemed to improve early is their 3-point shooting. Cade Cunningham is carrying over his playoff 3-point shooting with a career-high 37%, and Kevin Huerter , who struggled after coming from Chicago at midseason, is at a more-than-respectable clip of 38.5% (he shot 29% in 25 games last season). Duncan Robinson is No. 4 in makes, and the team collectively has risen to No. 6 in percentage (38.1). Their season high in triples in a game in 2025-26 was 18, a mark they've matched twice in the first two weeks. -- Vince Goodwill 3. Philadelphia 76ers 2026-27 record: 7-1 Previous ranking: 5 Next games: @ DET (Nov. 4), @ CLE (Nov. 6), @ CHI (Nov. 8), vs. BOS (Nov. 10) The Tyrese Maxey Show. Maxey has been Philly's best player while being on a team with two former MVPs, LeBron James and Joel Embiid , and a Finals MVP in Jaylen Brown . The 25-year-old leads the Sixers in scoring and has buoyed them late in games this season with explosive fourth quarters that have kept them winning. He leads the NBA in fourth-quarter scoring (11.0). "I just think he now feels -- like in a nonarrogant and even a humble way -- he knows he's really, really good," coach Nick Nurse said of Maxey. "And I'm not sure that was always the case." -- Kris Rhim 4. Boston Celtics 2026-27 record: 5-2 Previous ranking: 8 Next games: vs. MIL (Nov. 4), @ CHA (Nov. 6), @ MIL (Nov. 8), @ PHI (Nov. 10) They'll be just fine. The Celtics traded All-NBA forward Brown fresh off his best season for 36-year-old Paul George this offseason, a return that came as somewhat of a surprise considering George appears to be declining. But through the first two weeks, George has fit in with the Celtics seamlessly as the team has looked like a contender in the Eastern Conference. George is averaging 20.7 points, six rebounds and five assists. Coach Joe Mazzulla recently praised George's impact for being "beyond what's happening on the offensive end," pointing to George's leadership. -- Rhim 5. San Antonio Spurs 2026-27 record: 5-2 Previous ranking: 9 Next games: vs. DAL (Nov. 4), @ SAC (Nov. 6), @ POR (Nov. 7), @ PHX (Nov. 9) Still working through kinks. San Antonio expected that, coming into the season, it would have to work through some hiccups with its new starting lineup, but Spurs coach Mitch Johnson is committed to seeing it through. And slowly, the group is starting to deliver on the promise Johnson saw when pondering whether to put them all together. Of course, Victor Wembanyama is at the center of it all, and San Antonio's dynamic guards are finding more ways to get him shots closer to the basket. Wembanyama currently leads the NBA in made alley-oops, averaging 3.8 per game, more than twice the average of any other player. -- Wright 6. Memphis Grizzlies 2026-27 record: 6-1 Previous ranking: 14 Next games: vs. IND (Nov. 4), vs. OKC (Nov. 6), @ TOR (Nov. 9) Kleiman "conviction" is confirmed. After last season's trade deadline, Grizzlies general manager Zach Kleiman expressed confidence in what was left in Memphis after jettisoning key players -- Desmond Bane the previous summer and later Jaren Jackson Jr . -- from a roster previously expected to contend for years to come. Kleiman moved the final player, Ja Morant , in June. But on that February day, Kleiman discussed his "conviction" in "pivoting to a younger build" that was "not going to be some drawn-out five-year process." Perhaps he was right, considering Memphis' 6-1 start behind young players such as Cameron Boozer and Cedric Coward taking on major roles alongside a resurgent Ty Jerome . -- Wright 7. Los Angeles Lakers 2026-27 record: 6-2 Previous ranking: 6 Next games: @ SAC (Nov. 4), vs. POR (Nov. 6), @ DET (Nov. 8), @ ATL (Nov. 9) Luka's on a heater It's hard to imagine a better start to the season for the Slovenian sharpshooter, leading the league in scoring with 38.3 points per game on percentage splits of 49.7/42.7/88.7. After he scored 42 in a rout of the Heat on Monday, Giannis Antetokounmpo wondered aloud whether Doncic wasn't just establishing himself as the best scorer in today's game, but rather the best to ever put the ball in the basket in the history of the game. Most encouraging for L.A., the points have come with wins. The Lakers are 6-2 out of the gates. -- Dave McMenamin 8. Portland Trail Blazers 2026-27 record: 5-1 Previous ranking: 10 Next games: @ PHX (Nov. 4), @ LAL (Nov. 6), vs. SA (Nov. 7), vs. OKC (Nov. 10) Rolling along without Ja. While critics of Portland's offseason trade for Morant questioned his fit in a crowded backcourt, it pays to have extra depth in the modern NBA. Countless teams are struggling to cope with early-season injuries to key players, but the Blazers have maintained their positive momentum despite losing Morant to a strained hamstring after only four games. Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard kept the offense humming throughout a convincing road win over Denver on Monday. Meanwhile, Scoot Henderson has stepped into Morant's starting spot to bolster Portland's perimeter defense, and veteran Jrue Holiday has thrived as a selfless sixth man. -- Ben Golliver 9. Cleveland Cavaliers 2026-27 record: 4-3 Previous ranking: 13 Next games: @ OKC (Nov. 4), vs. PHI (Nov. 6), vs. NYK (Nov. 7), @ CHA (Nov. 9) Still figuring themselves out. The good news is Cleveland has more wins than losses; the bad news is the Cavaliers haven't looked that smooth in the process, with Peyton Watson in particular struggling to jell with his new squad. Cleveland has plenty of time to find its form, but the early returns are mixed rather than overwhelmingly positive. -- Zach Kram 10. Oklahoma City Thunder 2026-27 record: 5-2 Previous ranking: 1 Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 4), @ MEM (Nov. 6), vs. WAS (Nov. 7), @ POR (Nov. 10) Injuries are adding up. The injuries to four All-Defensive players -- Jalen Williams , Cason Wallace , Chet Holmgren and Alex Caruso -- have robbed the Thunder of one of their offensive superpowers. The Thunder have averaged only 11.8 points off of turnovers in the past four games, which ranks third to last in the league during that span. By contrast, Oklahoma City led the NBA in points off of turnovers in each of the past three seasons. -- Tim MacMahon 11. Minnesota Timberwolves 2026-27 record: 5-3 Previous ranking: 2 Next games: @ HOU (Nov. 4), @ NO (Nov. 6), vs. UTAH (Nov. 8) Come back soon, Ant. The Timberwolves are hanging tough without Anthony Edwards , who is expected to sit out two months after undergoing a knee procedure . Without their franchise guard, the Timberwolves struggled to sustain their newfound happy-go-lucky vibes during losses to the Warriors and Spurs. But Minnesota did take care of business against the Clippers and Bucks -- two projected bottom-dwellers -- to keep its head above water. Ayo Dosunmu , who signed a five-year, $112 million contract this summer, will get the chance to prove his worth while starting in place of Edwards. -- Golliver 12. Golden State Warriors 2026-27 record: 5-3 Previous ranking: 27 Next games: vs. MIA (Nov. 5), vs. ORL (Nov. 7), vs. NO (Nov. 9) Yaxel Lendeborg has arrived. The No. 11 pick in June's draft has already scored 26, 26, 31 and 37 points in his first two weeks in the NBA. His latest outburst, which included six 3s, came in a win over the LA Clippers in which Stephen Curry and Draymond Green rested. This Warriors team just followed an 0-3 start with a sudden five-game surge, and Curry, after the fifth straight win, was asked what changed. "Yax," Curry said. The Warriors didn't win five straight all of last season. The Warriors drafted a 24-year-old, 6-foot-10 power wing who has immediately looked like a top-30ish player in the NBA. "Changes everything," coach Steve Kerr said. -- Anthony Slater 13. Dallas Mavericks 2026-27 record: 4-3 Previous ranking: 22 Next games: @ SA (Nov. 4), vs. UTAH (Nov. 6), vs. BKN (Nov. 8), vs. IND (Nov. 9) Flagg is taking off. Cooper Flagg 's ascent to becoming an elite scorer hit a speed bump in Monday's loss to the previously winless Kings, when the 19-year-old went 3-of-19 from the field. Flagg is still averaging 25.2 points this season. The only players in NBA history to average that many points at age 20 or younger: LeBron James , Luka Doncic , Kevin Durant and Zion Williamson . -- MacMahon 14. Toronto Raptors 2026-27 record: 4-3 Previous ranking: 7 Next games: @ DEN (Nov. 4), @ MIL (Nov. 6), vs. MEM (Nov. 9) Life without Kawhi, again. After reacquiring Leonard in a trade this offseason , the Raptors have already been forced to deal with the reality of Leonard: one of the league's best players who has been consistently sidelined because of left knee swelling. Still, the Raptors have remained afloat thanks to Scottie Barnes , who is ninth in steals per game (2.1) and 13th in scoring (24.4), and a historically suffocating defense that leads the league with 20.9 turnovers per game. -- Rhim 15. Denver Nuggets 2026-27 record: 3-3 Previous ranking: 12 Next games: vs. TOR (Nov. 4), @ IND (Nov. 7), @ HOU (Nov. 9) A lone bright spot. Among several problems that emerged for the Nuggets in last April's first-round flameout to the injured Minnesota Timberwolves, Jamal Murray 's lack of production was perhaps the most destructive. He shot 35.7% in the series, 26.2% on 3s and petered out in a 12-point elimination Game 6, missing 13 of 17 shots. That memory appears flushed to open the season. Murray is one of the hottest scorers in the NBA, averaging 27.3 points and making more than 50% of his 3s. Even so, the Nuggets are a wobbly 3-3, with a remarkably average offense, considering they still have Nikola Jokic manning the middle. They led the NBA with a 121.2 offensive rating last season. They're currently 16th at 112.6. -- Slater 16. Washington Wizards 2026-27 record: 4-3 Previous ranking: 18 Next games: vs. ATL (Nov. 4), @ ATL (Nov. 6), @ OKC (Nov. 7), @ DET (Nov. 9) The ADs look great. Anthony Davis has been Washington's best player, averaging 23.0 points and 9.1 rebounds, and AJ Dybantsa -- whose two initials are the same as the veteran big man's -- has averaged 19 points on 50% shooting in his first three games in the NBA. That's everything Washington could have wanted from the two No. 1 picks so far. -- Kram 17. New York Knicks 2026-27 record: 3-4 Previous ranking: 16 Next games: vs. CHI (Nov. 4), @ CLE (Nov. 7), vs. MIL (Nov. 10) The Mikal Bridges question. The curious case of Bridges continues to start the season, culminating in him playing only 16 minutes against the Nets on Monday night. It's a small sample size, but he's averaging career lows in scoring and efficiency, and even his 3-point attempts are down. The Knicks made a concerted effort to get him going, but it seemed futile. "He's just got to keep playing," Knicks coach Mike Brown said. "Everybody goes through those ups and downs throughout the course of the season, and obviously, it's the beginning of the season right now, so he's got to find his way. "When you're in a funk, you got to find one or two things to hold your hat on." -- Goodwill 18. Atlanta Hawks 2026-27 record: 4-4 Previous ranking: 15 Next games: @ WAS (Nov. 4), vs. WAS (Nov. 6), vs. BKN (Nov. 7), vs. LAL (Nov. 9) Taking advantage of circumstances. The standings will show Atlanta winning games against Cleveland and Indiana in the past week. What won't appear is Cleveland playing in the second night of a back-to-back and Indiana having only six healthy players . The Pacers became the first team to have six players available this early in the season since the 1948 Boston Celtics. -- Bobby Marks 19. Miami Heat 2026-27 record: 2-5 Previous ranking: 24 Next games: @ LAC (Nov. 4), @ GS (Nov. 5), @ SAC (Nov. 8), @ UTAH (Nov. 10) No D, no chance . A team with Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo should not have the fourth-worst defense in the NBA. But through the first two weeks of the season, Miami has given up an average of 125 points in their five losses. In their loss to the Lakers on Monday, Miami gave up 138 points, its most this season. This was the 10th time in franchise history (and the second time this season) the Heat have given up at least 130 points. -- Marks 20. Charlotte Hornets 2026-27 record: 3-5 Previous ranking: 17 Next games: @ BKN (Nov. 4), vs. BOS (Nov. 6), vs. CLE (Nov. 9) They need their guards. Coby White played 16 minutes in his first game of the season Monday while Kon Knueppel has yet to debut , and the Hornets' offense has suffered without that starting backcourt. Sion James (28% shooting, 22% on 3s) and Dennis Schroder (37% shooting, 18% on 3s) started in their absence but didn't do much to put pressure on opposing defenses. -- Kram 21. Orlando Magic 2026-27 record: 2-5 Previous ranking: 20 Next games: @ PHX (Nov. 5), @ GS (Nov. 7), @ SAC (Nov. 10) No home-court identity. The two road wins against New York and Toronto proved that Orlando can compete with the top teams in the East. Playing at home is a different story. The Magic capped the second week of the regular season with home losses to Boston and Washington. They are now 0-4 and one of five teams without a home win. They trail only Milwaukee, Charlotte and Brooklyn with the worst point differential in home games. -- Marks 22. New Orleans Pelicans 2026-27 record: 3-4 Previous ranking: 26 Next games: vs. UTAH (Nov. 4), vs. MIN (Nov. 6), @ LAC (Nov. 8), @ GS (Nov. 9) No Dejounte, no problem . After a concerning 0-4 start, New Orleans' stunning overtime victory over previously unbeaten Memphis on Monday was its third straight win without guard Dejounte Murray (personal reasons). Though Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley opened the season with an undersized starting backcourt featuring Murray and Jeremiah Fears , his team's offensive efficiency has improved by nearly 10 points during Murray's absence. Herbert Jones and Karlo Matkovic have added more size and versatility to the new-look starting lineup during the winning streak, leaving Mosley with some difficult decisions once Murray returns. -- Golliver 23. Indiana Pacers 2026-27 record: 2-6 Previous ranking: 11 Next games: @ MEM (Nov. 4), vs. DEN (Nov. 7), @ DAL (Nov. 9) Injury bug bites again. It wasn't bad enough that Tyrese Haliburton is out for at least two weeks because of a hamstring injury . Indiana's entire starting five sat out Monday's game, albeit the second night of a back-to-back, giving the Pacers visions of last season when injuries to Haliburton started a wave throughout the roster. Indiana will have to survive this early-season slog and hope for a throwback to two years ago. The Pacers were under .500 in mid-December before turning their season around in January with a run that carried them to the Finals. -- Jamal Collier 24. Phoenix Suns 2026-27 record: 1-4 Previous ranking: 19 Next games: vs. POR (Nov. 4), vs. ORL (Nov. 5), vs. HOU (Nov. 7), vs. SA (Nov. 9), vs. LAC (Nov. 10) Who's doing the rebounding? The Suns are 29th in the league in rebounds per game, securing only 39.6 boards a night. In related news, Phoenix is 27th in opponent's offensive rebounds allowed per game (14.2). Both are contributing to the Suns ranking dead last in defensive rating, allowing 124 points per 100 possessions. We knew the center position was a soft spot for this roster heading into the season, but it has been even worse than expected so far. -- McMenamin 25. LA Clippers 2026-27 record: 1-6 Previous ranking: 23 Next games: vs. MIA (Nov. 4), vs. NO (Nov. 8), @ PHX (Nov. 10) Six-game losing streak. After routing the Sacramento Kings by 25 points to start the season, the Clippers lost their next six straight by an average margin 12.7 points. Their offense has been hard to come by. Their leading scorer, Darius Garland , is averaging 20.1 points on 43.5% shooting, and their second-leading scorer, Rui Hachimura , is averaging 13.4 points on just 36.9% shooting. Maybe their next game against the Heat will be just what they need -- considering how rough the Heat's defense has been so far (27th in the league). -- McMenamin 26. Utah Jazz 2026-27 record: 1-6 Previous ranking: 21 Next games: @ NO (Nov. 4), @ DAL (Nov. 6), @ MIN (Nov. 8), vs. MIA (Nov. 10) Lauri Markkanen 's slow start. Utah needs Markkanen to return to his All-Star form. The 7-footer is averaging 16.5 points and shooting only 38.5% from the field, including 34.3% from 3-point range. It doesn't help that Markkanen is now dealing with a sprained right (shooting) wrist as he attempts to establish a rhythm. -- MacMahon 27. Chicago Bulls 2026-27 record: 1-6 Previous ranking: 25 Next games: @ NYK (Nov. 4), vs. PHI (Nov. 8) Beginning of a rebuild. This is what step one of a rebuild looks like. The Bulls knew they had a long way to go when their new front office arrived this summer, and the start of the season has confirmed as much. They have one win in their first seven games and haven't been super competitive against a tough schedule (they played Toronto with Kawhi Leonard , Boston twice, and will face the Knicks and Sixers for a second time later this week). Chicago ranks in the bottom five in both offensive and defensive efficiency and, outside of Caleb Wilson 's strong start, not much has gone right so far. -- Collier 28. Milwaukee Bucks 2026-27 record: 1-6 Previous ranking: 28 Next games: @ BOS (Nov. 4), vs. TOR (Nov. 6), vs. BOS (Nov. 8), @ NYK (Nov. 10) Who survives the season? After trading their superstar over the summer, the Bucks have an ill-fitting roster that is clearly in transition. Milwaukee is looking for a new identity and the start of the season has not been encouraging with this many new players on the roster. So, how will Milwaukee continue to remake its roster going forward? What does the future hold for some Bucks veterans, including Myles Turner , Kyle Kuzma and Tyler Herro , who are not on the same timeline as some of the Bucks' other young players, namely No. 10 pick Brayden Burries ? -- Collier 29. Brooklyn Nets 2026-27 record: 1-6 Previous ranking: 29 Next games: vs. CHA (Nov. 4), @ ATL (Nov. 7), @ DAL (Nov. 8) Playing with good intentions. That's about all you can say about the Nets at this point. They've held late leads, they've competed. At times, like Monday, Brooklyn gets a little scattered or too heavily dependent on Julius Randle to retrieve the team from the muck and it has a quicksand effect. But on the positive side, the Nets rank No. 3 in the NBA with nearly 40% of their scoring coming from 3-point range, and No. 7 in makes at 14.3 per game. -- Goodwill 30. Sacramento Kings 2026-27 record: 1-6 Previous ranking: 30 Next games: vs. LAL (Nov. 4), vs. SA (Nov. 6), vs. MIA (Nov. 8), vs. ORL (Nov. 10) The rookie isn't shy. Here are Darius Acuff Jr .'s shot attempts in his first seven NBA games: 24, 26, 23, 20, 26, 25, 21. Everyone assumed the rebuilding Kings would give their 19-year-old point guard the ultimate green light. Acuff has accepted, slamming down the gas pedal. His first four games were inefficient. His past three have been encouraging -- 35-of-72 overall plus a 14-assist effort. Acuff's most recent outing also led the previously 0-6 Kings to their first win. He had 25 points in Dallas and closed it out with a flurry, scoring seven in the last five minutes, including a dagger 3-pointer over Cooper Flagg. -- Slater

teamStories.title: Draymond Green scolds Spurs for ‘disheartening' actions after NBA Finals loss
teamStories.summary: Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green criticized the San Antonio Spurs for actions following their NBA Finals loss to the New York Knicks.
teamStories.detailText: Draymond Green scolds Spurs for ‘disheartening' actions after NBA Finals loss originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area The San Antonio Spurs learned a few hard lessons during their 2026 NBA Finals loss to the New York Knicks, and to hear Draymond Green tell it, they have another still to go. The Warriors forward took to his podcast , “The Draymond Green Show,” to admonish the young Spurs for what he called a “disheartening” lack of leadership as the team left the floor following Saturday’s series-ending defeat without offering any formal congratulations to the victorious Knicks. “Oh, by the way, y’all ain’t going to come shake [ Jalen Brunson ’s] hand?” Green said. “No problem. What’s the first thing Jalen Brunson did? Beeline to [Spurs coach] Mitch Johnson . Respect. Much respect. I would have loved for the Spurs players to be there for them to shake [the Knicks’] hands. They walked off. That was disappointing, a bit disappointing.” New York secured its first NBA championship since 1973 by beating San Antonio in five games, with the title-decider coming on the Spurs’ home floor. When the final buzzer sounded on a 94-90 Knicks win, nearly every Spurs player—including star center Victor Wembanyama —left the floor immediately. Per reports , only the San Antonio coaching staff and backup center Luke Kornet remained to offer their respects to New York players. “The reason it was disappointing is because when you go ‘mano y mano,’ toe to toe, blow for blow with a team and they get the better of you, those that become champions look them in their eyes and say ‘respect.’” Green said of the Spurs’ postgame exit. “And then you go to the locker room. That’s what those that become champions do…Look your killer in the face.” Green did give San Antonio some grace, conceding that the team is generally very young and lacks the veteran presence that might have helped avoid what he saw as a lapse in sportsmanship. “To see [the Spurs] walk off the court, it was disheartening. I’ll blame it on youth,” Green said. “I’ll blame it on lacking the leader to show them that ‘hey, this is what you do. Not walk off.’ I blame it on that. “There’s a way to win and there’s a way to lose. And walking off the court, not looking your killer in his eyes, ain’t the way to lose…I hate it. I hate when people do it. And I hated to see those young Spurs do it because I actually think they’re capable of doing something special…and I would urge those young Spurs [to] reach out to Jalen Brunson however you can. Reach out to Karl-Anthony Towns however you can. Reach out to Josh Hart , however you can. You tell [those] dudes ‘congratulations.’” The Knicks, for their part, didn’t appear all that concerned. The celebration was ON in the @nyknicks locker room last night after winning their first NBA Championship in 53 years 🏆🍾 pic.twitter.com/3aprwZbaiT — NBA (@NBA) June 14, 2026 Download and follow the Dubs Talk Podcast

stories.title: Lions' Jack Campbell has full movement in lower body after neck injury
stories.summary: Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell released a statement Wednesday saying he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with movement in his upper body as he recovers from a neck injury, suffered in Sunday's game.
stories.detailText: Detroit Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell released a statement Wednesday saying he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with movement in his upper body as he recovers from a neck injury, suffered in Sunday's game. Campbell, who remains hospitalized, was placed on a backboard and carted off the field early in the fourth quarter of a 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. He was alert and breathing when he was taken to the hospital. "I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body," Campbell said in a statement. "I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better." Lions coach Dan Campbell said it was powerful that Jack Campbell updated his improving condition himself, shortly before the team's previously scheduled news conferences with coaches and players. "That's good news. That's positive news," Dan Campbell said. "We're all thankful for that." Campbell was face down on the turf and not moving Sunday after hitting tight end T.J. Hockenson for his third tackle of the game. Campbell was evaluated by medical personnel before being strapped to a board and carefully lifted onto the cart to a round of applause. Detroit's entire team and most of the coaching staff surrounded the cart. "I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field," Jack Campbell said in his statement. "I know those were difficult moments, and I'm incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I'll never forget." The former Iowa star was drafted by the Lions with the 18th overall pick in 2023. Last season, Campbell was an All-Pro selection after becoming the first NFL player in seven years to have 150-plus tackles and at least five sacks and three forced fumbles. The Lions signed Campbell last May to a four-year contract extension that runs through the 2030 season. The Lions (5-2) play at Miami (1-6) on Sunday. Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.title: Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes hasn't run QB sneak since '19 season
stories.summary: The Chiefs continue to struggle in short-yardage rushing situations, with the team having not attempted a sneak of any kind since the 2023 season.
stories.detailText: KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Chiefs coach Andy Reid gave no indication Wednesday that he plans to utilize any kind of sneak to help improve the offense's struggles in short-yardage situations this season. Entering Sunday's game against the New York Jets , the Chiefs have converted just 20 of 34 chances in which they needed 2 yards or less on third- and fourth-down snaps. Not once has quarterback Patrick Mahomes or another skill-position player attempted a sneak. "Yeah, I think that's going to be our first call [Sunday]," Reid jokingly said with a blank facial expression. The last time the Chiefs attempted a sneak of any kind was Week 6 of the 2023 season, when tight end Noah Gray attempted one on a fake field goal play on fourth-and-2. The Denver Broncos held Gray to a 1-yard gain. Mahomes hasn't run a sneak since Week 7 of the 2019 season, when he suffered a dislocated right kneecap on the play, which forced him to miss two games. Kansas City is the lone NFL team not to have run a quarterback sneak since then. Last Sunday, facing third-and-goal at the 1-yard line with nine seconds remaining against the Broncos, Mahomes got under center and handed the ball off to running back Kenneth Walker III , who was tackled by safety JL Skinner for no gain. Mahomes said he didn't consider calling an audible for a sneak on the play as the Broncos' goal-line stand clinched a 28-24 victory. "Well, if I do that, it better work," Mahomes said, smiling and laughing. "I understand people, when you watch the film and see stuff, you want [us] to go out there and make it happen. Obviously, the play call is what we called, and we wanted to execute that play. They were able to stunt and get people in position to where Kenneth wasn't able to get going downhill and score a touchdown. "If I do call my own number, it's got to work. That's something I'll think about in the future." Despite Walker's success this season -- he's third in the league with 770 rushing yards -- the Chiefs have not been efficient in short-yardage situations. The issue is even more glaring when closer to the goal line. When the ball is inside the 5, the Chiefs have managed only two touchdowns on 13 rushing attempts for an NFL-worst 14% success rate. "It's something we've been better at in the past years," Mahomes said. "Obviously, this year, we haven't been able to execute in those situations. It always comes down to kind of one guy here or there and just not being on the same page. "We have to continue to be more and more physical. We have to continue to be on the same page, understand what the defense is presenting to us, be able to communicate well then go out there and just make it happen. It's not always going to be pretty, but you've got to make it happen." The Chiefs could utilize backup quarterback Justin Fields in those situations; he converted on seven of his eight sneak attempts while with the Jets last season. Mahomes, however, made it clear he's willing to run the sneak if Reid gives him the opportunity. "I'm going to do whatever it takes to win," Mahomes said. "It's not like I'm scared to go out there and put my body on the line. That's how I've played. It's got me in trouble sometimes and sometimes it's helped the team."

stories.title: Dianna Russini gets out the word that she's coming back to work next week
stories.summary: The halfway point of the 2026 NFL season arrives this weekend.
stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_powerankings_261104","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"Power Rankings (Toyota)","duration":"622789","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_powerankings_261104","genre":"News, Trending","guid":"nbc_pft_powerankings_261104","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Buffalo Bills, Chicago Bears","title": "PFT Power Rankings: Bills remain at No. 1","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/nfl-power-rankings-bills-remain-at-no-1-buccaneers-land-at-no-18","availableDate":"2026-11-04T13:45:07Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} The halfway point of the 2026 NFL season arrives this weekend. Next week, Dianna Russini apparently will return to sports media. Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Russini has begun getting the word out to people in the league that she'll be returning to work "next week." It's unclear where she'll be working, or what she'll be doing. She resigned from The Athletic in April, one week after photos were published by the New York Post of Russini and Patriots coach Mike Vrabel at a resort in Arizona. In both her comments to the Post and her resignation letter to The Athletic, she denied that there was any type of impropriety. The Athletic conducted a review of her work. Its findings were released in early September. “Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic ’s standards,” wrote Mike Semel of The Athletic , who conducted the investigation. “Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed.” Beyond the relationship was the manner in which she handled the emergence of the controversy. "[W]hen first confronted with the photos by The New York Post ,” Semel wrote, “Russini waited two days before telling her editors and managers. She then told a story to explain the photos that did not align with facts, raising issues of trust.” Along the way, a strange story emerged regarding Russini being pulled over for texting while driving — made stranger by her decision to tell the story publicly and embellish the notion that she FaceTimed a head coach for help in getting out of the ticket. So if she'll be reporting again, she's need to restore her own credibility. Especially given the unique set of facts that resulted in her departure from The Athletic .

stories.title: Colts' Shane Steichen defends Jonathan Taylor usage, says RB will keep role
stories.summary: Jonathan Taylor will continue to play his usual role with the Colts despite being at the center of trade talks with multiple teams, Shane Steichen said.
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS -- Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor will continue to play his usual role despite being at the center of trade talks with multiple teams, coach Shane Steichen said Tuesday. Steichen was pressed about the organization's approach with Taylor, who played 38 snaps in the Colts' 42-7 loss Sunday to the Jacksonville Jaguars . Steichen said there has been no change to the Colts' plan for Taylor in Week 9 against the Dallas Cowboys . "There's a lot of stuff out there right now," Steichen said of speculation surrounding Taylor. "He's on our football team and he's excited for this opportunity to go play. He wants to go win this game." Taylor has attracted trade interest from numerous teams since the Colts (2-6) signaled in recent weeks that they are directing their focus toward the future. The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard last month and traded highly respected veterans Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week. Relatedly, receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade, though he also played last Sunday and is expected to play against Dallas. "I'm focused on now," Downs said Wednesday. "We play the Cowboys this week. We have practice today. We're trying to go out there and win. ... I've got to focus on now. That's what's most important." Steichen acknowledged the Arizona Cardinals ' recent decision to hold Marvin Harrison Jr . out of a game after a trade involving the receiver had been agreed to with the Houston Texans . But Steichen said there have been no conversations to that effect between him and the Colts' front office. "During this time of year, people are going to call," he said. "That's just part of the business. But, again, you've got to be a professional and show up to work."

stories.title: Harrison Butker is still the Chiefs’ kicker heading into Week 9
stories.summary: Head coach Andy Reid confirmed Kansas City is sticking with its longtime kicker for now.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, the Kansas City Chiefs brought in former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker to the practice squad after Harrison Butker’s shaky start to the season. Tucker impressed the Chiefs and special teams coordinator Dave Toub in his tryout, but will stay with the reserves for at least another week as the team continues to trust their guy. When Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star asked about the placekicking situation before Wednesday’s practice, head coach Andy Reid said there would be no change. “Harrison will be in, yeah,” Reid confirmed. The question comes after Butker missed a 54-yard field goal in the rainy fourth quarter of the close loss to the Denver Broncos ; he made a 45-yard field goal and converted on all three of his point-after attempts. He is 12-for-18 on field goals this year, tied for the lowest rate in the NFL among qualified kickers currently on an active roster; former Los Angeles Rams kicker Harrison Mevis (56%) is the only one with a lower rate. Butker has attempted the third-most 50-or-more-yard kicks in the league this year (7) but has made only two. Five of his six misses have come from long range, but he has also missed a 45-yard field goal and a point-after attempt through seven games. On offense, Reid shared that there is also “a good chance” that starting left guard Kingsley Suamataia will be in after being benched (for an unclear reason) in the Week 8 loss to Denver. He played five snaps on special teams, a notable difference from his benching in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders , another divisional road game. Veteran backup Mike Caliendo filled in for Suamataia in both games. In his most recent game, Caliendo allowed five pressures — including a sack and two quarterback hits — over 68 snaps at left guard, according to Pro Football Focus . It was also a woeful performance against a Broncos defense that Kansas City ran all over in the season-opening matchup. With a strong indication that Suamataia will be back in the lineup, it feels like the team knows he is the better player. So why has a coach’s decision kept him off the field in two crucial games this season? It feels like we’ll never get that answer.

stories.title: Todd Monken: Deshaun Watson not ruled out yet, but Shedeur Sanders preparing to start
stories.summary: Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol after self-reporting symptoms on Tuesday.
stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_shedeur_261104","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"262929","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_shedeur_261104","genre":"News","guid":"nbc_pft_shedeur_261104","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Cleveland Browns","title": "Shedeur’s days with Browns feel numbered","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/shedeur-sanders-days-with-cleveland-browns-feel-numbered","availableDate":"2026-11-04T13:35:35Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol after self-reporting symptoms on Tuesday. Head coach Todd Monken told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that Watson hasn’t necessarily been ruled out for Sunday’s game against New Orleans. But the club is preparing Shedeur Sanders to start. “What I would say is, credit to Deshaun — after the game, [he] felt fine. Monday night, started feeling a little bit, little bit of a headache, and came in Tuesday and, you know, reported,” Monken said, via transcript from the team. “So, credit to him for someone who really loves playing the game. And so, he is in the protocol. And Shedeur will take the reps today with the ones.” Monken admitted that it’s “a little more difficult” for a quarterback to play on Sunday after missing practice due to a concussion. But Monken and the team will let the process play out. “I mean, there’s a long time between now and then, right? I mean, look where the Ravens are at. And you don’t know as the week goes on what could happen,” Monken said. “It’s not ideal, right? It’s not ideal for any player to go through a week and not practice and then play. We know that. But every situation is different.” Monken noted that Watson can participate in the team’s meetings to help him stay prepared in the event that he gets cleared. The team has been game-planning with the idea that Sanders will start. But Monken said the game plan won’t change much if it’s Sanders or Watson behind center. “I don’t see the way [it would change], because the rest of the guys are the same, and they’re similar in some ways,” Monken said. “Some things, you know, Shedeur’s skill set is different than Deshaun’s, but still very similar in terms of what we do. We can’t change that dramatically.” Either way, Watson is expected to still be the starter when he is cleared. “Yeah, I didn’t assume I’d get that question. Yeah, he’s been our starter for eight games. I would assume he’s still our starter,” Monken said. “I don’t — I’m thinking about Wednesday. But I’m not — I’m really thinking about today and watching Shedeur play today.” So far this season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards with seven touchdowns and three interceptions. He’s been sacked a league-high 33 times. His eight games this season are the most he’s played in a year for the Browns since arriving on the club in 2022. Last season, Sanders completed 56.6 percent of his throws for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight games with seven starts.

stories.detailText: The Lions were obviously without linebacker Jack Campbell at practice on Wednesday and two other key defensive players were also on the sideline as the team worked to get ready to face the Dolphins. stories.title: Lions, Dolphins Week 9 injury report:
stories.summary: Taking a closer look at the Lions and Dolphins initial injury report for Week 9.
stories.detailText: Detroit Lions defensive back Brian Branch (32) warms up ahead of the game between Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions (5-2) are back on the road in Week 9, traveling to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6). The Lions held a walkthrough on Wednesday instead of a full practice, so all participation levels are estimates from the coaching staff based on how the player would have participated in a traditional practice. With that in mind, let’s look at Wednesday’s injury report and get you up to date on what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . Injured list updates RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back, IR) — expected to be out until December OL Giovanni Manu (undisclosed, NFI) — eligible to begin practicing at any time OL Ben Bartch (foot, IR) — eligible to begin practicing in Week 10 LB Devin White (forearm, IR) — eligible to begin practicing in Week 10 LB Jimmy Rolder (hamstring, IR) — Season-ending injury S Kerby Joseph (knee, PUP) — Injury evaluation clock started S Thomas Harper (ankle, IR) — Eligible to begin practicing at any time Rolder injured his hamstring last Sunday, and with the injury potentially requiring surgery, he’s being shut down for the remainder of the season. While that ends his rookie season, the good news is he should be able to return in 2027. Jack Campbell update I wanted to take a moment to talk about Jack Campbell, as most Lions fans are anxiously awaiting updates on his status and wondering about his future, both on and off the field. First, in case you missed it, Jack Campbell released a statement earlier on Wednesday ; here’s an excerpt (emphasis is the author’s): “I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body . I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.” Jack is still on the 53-man roster and hasn’t been moved to injured reserve, but it would be improper to speculate why a move has or hasn’t been made at this time. The team typically takes their time in these situations, so it’s important to be patient right now and not make assumptions either way. Estimated n o practice C Cade Mays (ankle) — Injured in Week 8 — Preparing for Juice Scruggs to start EDGE DJ Wonnum (concussion) — Injured in Week 8 LB Jack Campbell (neck) — Injured in Week 8 CB D.J. Reed (hip) — Injured in Week 8 Mays reportedly has a “low” ankle injury, which typically sidelines players from one to six weeks (high ankle injuries usually last four to 12 weeks), and while we don’t know how long this will sideline the Lions’ starting center, Dan Campbell did note that he missing Wednesday’s practice was planned and Thursday’s practice could also be in jeopardy. For now, the team is preparing to turn to Juice Scruggs against the Dolphins. Wonnum is in the NFL’s concussion protocol and must pass a series of steps before he can move forward. Every player deals with head injuries differently, so we will have to wait and see how he is able to handle the increasing stressors deployed in the protocol. Reed was forced out of the Vikings game late, and while he didn’t return, he was available in the locker room after the game, which is typically a good sign for his injury. The Lions will likely take it slow with their top corner this week. Estimated limited practice RB Jacob Saylors (neck) — Injured in Week 8 WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) — Injured in Week 8 LB Amen Ogbongbemiga (toe) — Injured in Week 8 S Kerby Joseph (knee, PUP) — Days remaining in injury evaluation clock: 13 S Brian Branch (concussion) — Injured in Week 8 Saylors was limited early in practices in Week 8 with a neck injury, and while he did not carry an injury designation into the game against the Vikings, he did exit with a reported neck injury. It’s unclear whether this is a new injury or a tweak of the existing one, but it’s not surprising to see him get early-week rest to allow more time to recover. Last week, St. Brown was dealing with an ankle injury, and now he’s dealing with a rib injury. He left Sunday’s game against the Vikings briefly but did not miss much time before returning. Ogbongbemiga is dealing with a toe injury, which could leave Detroit’s linebacker room a little short this week, but given he’s just listed as limited, there is plenty of time for him to recover. He could play a bigger special teams role this week, with Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske expected to play bigger defensive roles. On Tuesday, coach Dan Campbell discussed the timeline for Kerby Joseph, noting that he won’t play in Miami this weekend, as he’s still slowly acclimating back to football activities. “We’re going to try and give him some scout team reps. He’s not going to play this game,” Campbell said. “I know that (question) was coming. He’s not playing vs. Miami. He’s just going to get some reps in practice.” Branch, like Wonnum, must go through the NFL’s structured concussion protocol, but an estimated limited practice is a positive sign he could play this week. stories.title: Coach: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold ruled out with quad injury, is week-to-week
stories.summary: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will miss Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals because of a quad injury, coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday.
stories.detailText: RENTON, Wash. -- Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will miss the team's game against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday due to a quad injury, coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday. Darnold is week-to-week and will not be placed on injured reserve, per Macdonald. He said Darnold has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders . The Seahawks' plan is for backup Drew Lock to start against Arizona, but he's still dealing with an injury to his throwing elbow that caused him to be inactive the last two games. Macdonald acknowledged the possibility that Seattle may have to turn to QB3 Jalen Milroe depending on how Lock progresses. "We'll be getting both guys ready to play," Macdonald said. "We've got full confidence in those guys, and we have a plan in place and we'll go execute it." Seattle may be adding another quarterback this week, per Macdonald. Darnold injured his quad on the final drive of the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday night, which dropped the reigning Super Bowl champions to 4-4. Macdonald said he also suffered a cracked rib on the second play of the game, when he was hit hard while throwing by blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon . Macdonald wasn't aware of the rib injury until after the game, he said. Darnold went 17 of 34 passing for 188 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against Chicago. He was sacked three times and took six official QB hits. His off-target percentage of 29.4% was his highest in the six games he's played since he returned in Week 3 from a glute injury. "This guy, he's tough as nails," Macdonald said. "I just asked if I could share this, but he cracked his rib on the second play of the game. So he's playing the whole game without even making a thing of it and playing his tail off and competing. I think it's worth noting how tough this guy is. He'll be back sooner than later, I'm sure." Macdonald said Darnold could likely play through the cracked rib if not for the quad injury. They're the latest setbacks in what's been a tumultuous season for the quarterback. He suffered a glute injury on the fifth play of the season opener, which caused him to miss the remainder of that game and the following week. "I know it's a challenge, but I've got a lot of respect for how he goes through these things because he goes through it," Macdonald said. "There's no blink, there's no flinch. It's a very matter-of-fact, attacking mentality, which I think that's reflective of the rest of our team, which I appreciate." Since returning in Week 3, Darnold has thrown nine interceptions in six games. He's completed just over 60% of his passes in that span, with 10 touchdown passes and a Total QBR of 50.8 that ranks 22nd. Lock, meanwhile, did not commit a turnover while playing most of the first two games. The eighth-year veteran completed nearly 73% of his passes and posted a Total QBR of 82.5 that ranked sixth in that span. Three of his four touchdown passes came in a 31-7 win over Arizona in Week 2, which moved Seattle to 2-0. Lock was listed as limited on all nine injury reports the Seahawks released from Weeks 6-8, starting on Oct. 11. He was questionable for the last two games before being ruled inactive, though he dressed both times as the emergency third quarterback. He was not seen throwing alongside Darnold and Milroe during warmups before either game. "He's able to throw," Macdonald said of Lock. "How much, we're working through that right now. But that's the best way to put it ... He's going to throw the ball throughout the week, but we're just going to manage it. He's not going to take 8,000 throws." Lock suffered the injury during a rainy practice, per Macdonald. He did not specify the date. "It's an elbow injury," Macdonald said. "All the fancy names, I can't explain that to you, but he hasn't throw much." The Seahawks drafted Milroe in the third round in 2025 with a plan to take advantage of his running ability in specialty packages while he developed as a passer. But after early fumbling issues, he hasn't seen the field during a regular-season game since Week 5 of last year. Macdonald said Lock and Milroe will be "splitting reps for a certain amount of time" this week. They're holding a walk-through Wednesday. "I think we've just got to take it day by day at this time," he said. "But Jalen will take some practice reps as well. Today's a slow day, so it's kind of hard to tell. We have a plan for Drew to get some live throws later, but I think it's just one of those things where we kind of have to work it day-in and day-out and figure out what's the best way to get him to Sunday." The Seahawks' 17-point loss to Chicago was their most lopsided defeat since December of 2024. They played without outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) and left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), then lost defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) in the second half. Macdonald said all four have a chance to play against Arizona.

stories.title: Ravens discussion: instant reactions to the Jacoby Brissett trade
stories.summary: Baltimore Beatdown’s staff gives their instant reactions to the Ravens’ trade for Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals.
stories.detailText: Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) takes the field before they play the Denver Broncos at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Oct. 25, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Baltimore Ravens are acquiring Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, adding some much-needed quarterback depth after potential season-ending injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to the move, and be sure to add yours in the comments section below! Nikhil Mehta I have long been a Jacoby Brissett fan. Turns out, so is Eric DeCosta! This is hardly a surprising trade considering the Ravens’ injury crisis at quarterback, and Brissett is exactly the type of bridge passer I expected the team to pick up. Look, we all like Joe Fagnano, but the undrafted rookie out of UConn simply is not ready to command an NFL offense. Fans will debate if the Ravens should even be trying to win games for the rest of the season, but this franchise was never going to throw in the towel. Brissett can provide a base level of play for as long as the Ravens need it. Keeping the team’s playoff hopes alive is another question entirely. Mark Myers This trade seemed likely on Sunday night, but became nailed on as soon as Arizona announced Brissett would drop to QB3 on their depth chart. Although his season has been much worse than 2025 (when he had a 23/8 TD/INT ratio), he can push the ball down the field and feed the Ravens’ weapons better than any of the current healthy options could. Compensation may take a while to be reported, but I suspect it won’t be anything above a 5th-round pick, maybe as low as a 6th-round pick going the other way. I’m just hoping this offense is watchable. Thankfully, Brissett’s debut is set to be against the Chargers. Maybe a win against Los Angeles in primetime can give the team a spark. Zach Canter I’m not a fan of this. My guess is this moves means the Ravens brass is fairly confident Lamar Jackson will return this season and they want a veteran quarterback capable of keeping them within striking distance of a playoff spot. Otherwise, this truly makes no sense. In my opinion, even if Jackson is capable of coming back this year, I still think it makes no sense. This team is riddled with issues, front and center being the offensive line. While I still think it can be a good unit if they can get the desired starting five on the field, which has happened for less than a quarter of total eight games, it’s still a question mark. The defense is still highly inconsistent. Their coaching staff seems to be young and learning as they go, which is fine and makes sense. But none of this adds up to a Super Bowl contending team. I am of the belief that the Ravens should be selling tradeable pieces at the deadline (Humphrey, Stanley, Andrews, Henry, Campbell, Washington, etc), locked 100% in on figuring out the Lamar Jackson extension, and building towards a massive roster overhaul to give Jesse Minter a team in his vision for 2027. Even if this trade is for as little as a 6th round pick, I don’t love it. If it’s for a 5th or more, I absolutely hate it and we should call DeCosta’s priorities of the future into question, as well as his job. Dustin Cox The Ravens had to make a move to get another competent quarterback in the building and Brissett perhaps made the most sense of their options. Brissett can hopefully elevate the Ravens’ offense to watchable status, but I don’t expect him to move the needle very much in terms of winning games. If Lamar Jackson is able to come back at some point this season, then Brissett can hopefully keep the team afloat and in the playoff hunt, but my expectations for the rest of the season are about as low as they can get at this moment. Acquiring an established veteran like Brissett at least sends the message to players on the team that the season isn’t being punted on entirely. Kevin McNelis Jacoby Brissett provides more veteran leadership than you would have otherwise had in this QB room, and he has enough of an arm and a deep ball that he’s serviceable. Not great, certainly not elite, but serviceable, which is more than what we can say about the unknowns of UDFA and practice squad crew that the Ravens had otherwise. The concern now would be what Baltimore gave up to get him (which hasn’t been disclosed as of this writing) and whether they can keep him upright and healthy. If this deal ends up being much ado about nothing as they move through a tough portion of their schedule, they can say they tried. From a roster-building standpoint, we may end up at Draft time grumbling about winning some games that didn’t help them move up the board, but the front office will always prioritize trying to compete if they think things can be salvaged.
